Article Title: Karnataka, Keralam governments launch E20 petrol quality checks amid ethanol blending concerns
Article Text:
The Keralam civil supplies department conducted inspections of petrol pumps in Kochi to examine the ethanol mix in E20 petrol. (Pic Credit: IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Keralam civil supplies department has inspected petrol pumps in Kochi to verify the ethanol content and density of E20 petrol amid growing concerns over alleged excessive ethanol blending in fuel.District civil supplies Officer Shaji PR said officials had collected six one-litre petrol samples during the inspection, of which two were sent to an analytical chemical laboratory in Kakinada for testing. The department is awaiting the laboratory reports."We conducted an inspection... We have inspected the details of the quantity of ethanol in the motor spirit, ordinary petrol. There were six samples at the rate of one litre taken. We sent two samples to an analytical chemical laboratory in Kakinada. We are waiting for the result," Shaji PR told ANI.The inspections come amid concerns raised by Karnataka Minister Rizwan Arshad over the possible impact of higher ethanol-blended petrol on vehicles. On Friday, he warned that fuel containing more than 20 per cent ethanol could damage vehicle components that are not designed to withstand higher concentrations.Addressing a press conference on November 6, Arshad said the Karnataka government had collected 63 fuel samples from different locations across every district, covering all major oil companies.The issue has also drawn criticism from Leader of opposition in the Lok sabha Rahul Gandhi, who questioned the centre over allegations that petrol sold in Karnataka contained ethanol beyond the prescribed 20 per cent limit. He sought to know when action would be taken against oil companies allegedly supplying fuel with excessive ethanol content.In a post on X, Gandhi described the alleged irregularity as an 'E20' scam, writing: "E20 turns into '420' (a scam) petrol theft from the public's vehicles. The Modi government claims that petrol contains 20% ethanol. The Karnataka government collected petrol samples from 7 districts and had them tested at an accredited laboratory."Karnataka's department of food, civil supplies, consumer affairs and legal metrology has claimed that motor spirit sold at certain retail outlets in the state contained ethanol concentrations ranging from 26 per cent to 31 per cent.However, the union ministry of petroleum and natural gas has rejected allegations of excessive ethanol blending, stating that all 893 samples of E20 petrol collected from public sector oil marketing companies across 27 states and Union Territories met the prescribed quality standards.The three state-run oil marketing companies, Indian oil corporation limited, Bharat petroleum corporation limited and Hindustan petroleum corporation limited, have also maintained that ethanol blending is a regulated and automated process carried out in accordance with statutory guidelines, rather than through manual intervention.
Article Summary: The Keralam civil supplies department has inspected petrol pumps in Kochi to verify the ethanol content and density of E20 petrol. The inspections come amid concerns raised by Karnataka Minister Rizwan Arshad over the possible impact of higher ethanol-blended petrol on vehicles.

Article Title: Jaishankar extends national day greetings to Cambodia, hails strong civilisational ties
Article Text:
S Jaishankar conveyed warm National Day wishes to Cambodia, celebrating the deep-rooted civilizational connections between the two countries. (Pic Credit: ANI)

External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Monday extended National Day greetings to Cambodia, highlighting the strong civilisational linkages shared by the two countries.In a post on X, Jaishankar said, “Greetings to DPM & FM Prak Sokhonn, the Government and people of Cambodia on their National Day. Value our strong bonds built on shared civilizational linkages. ”Jaishankar also highlighted the successful completion of the second edition of the Cambodia-India Bilateral Army Exercise (CINBAX-II) 2026, held in Cambodia from May 4 to 17.The 14-day joint military exercise between the Indian Army and the Royal Cambodian Army was conducted at the Techo Sen Phnom Thom Mreas Prov Royal Cambodian Air Force Training Centre in Kampong Speu Province.The exercise focused on joint planning and execution of tactical operations in a sub-conventional environment under the framework of Chapter VII of the United Nations mandate. It involved company-level joint training in a semi-urban setting.The Indian Army contingent comprised 120 personnel, primarily from a battalion of the Maratha Light Infantry Regiment, while the Cambodian contingent included 160 personnel from the Royal Cambodian Army.Training activities covered Command Post and Field Training Exercises, sniper training, mortar drills, tactical drone employment, combat first aid, urban operations, multi-domain operations and disaster relief.The exercise aimed to enhance interoperability through the exchange of tactics, techniques and procedures, while providing both contingents an opportunity to share operational experiences and best practices.The closing ceremony was held at the training centre following the successful completion of the exercise. Both contingents demonstrated professionalism and operational coordination during the comprehensive validation exercise.CINBAX-II 2026 further strengthened defence cooperation between India and Cambodia, enhanced mutual understanding and reinforced the growing partnership between the two countries in addressing evolving regional and global security challenges.(ANI)
Article Summary: S Jaishankar extended warm National Day greetings to Cambodia. He highlighted the strong civilisational linkages shared by the two countries. He also highlighted the successful completion of the second edition of the Cambodia- India Bilateral Army Exercise (CINBAX-II) 2026.

NEW DELHI: Referring to the contradictory orders given by Supreme Court in the matter of bail to the accused on the ground of delay in trial and long incarceration for UAPA offences, which have been referred to a larger bench for authoritative pronouncement, former student activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have moved SC for bail in 2020 Delhi riots cases.The accused submitted that two co-accused, including Tasleem Ahmed, were granted bail by SC on the grou-nd that determination of the issues by the larger bench would take time, and they could not be made to suffer continued incarceration.Seeking parity with the co-accused, Sharjeel Imam, who has already spent six years and nine months in custody, said in his petition, filed through advocate Fauzia Shakil, that two co-accused in the same FIR were released on interim bail by the court on May 22 under a principle which applies to him in greater degree.The accused moved SC after their plea for bail was rejected by the trial court and Delhi High Court on the ground that the apex court had purportedly set a deadline of Jan 5, 2027, for them to file a bail petition.The petition asked "whether the principle recognised by this Court in Tasleem Ahmed v. State order dated 22.05.2026, that an accused cannot be made to suffer continued incarceration merely because an important question of law has arisen for authoritative settlement, can be withheld from the petitioner alone by reference to the role attributed to him, when the question referred to concerns the correctness of the very judgment which declined his bail and relief in Tasleem Ahmed case was granted without any examination of role?"It further argued, "Whether liberty reserved by this Court in a judgment declining bail, to renew the prayer for bail at a defined point, operates as a bar upon the statutory jurisdiction of the Special Court and of the High Court to consider an application for bail founded on supervening circumstances be-fore that point, when the same paragraph of the judgment holds that pre-trial detention cannot be permitted to continue without regard to the progress of the trial and that Article 21 operates as a continuing check against continued incarceration without substantial progress of the trial?"
Article Summary: Former student activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have moved SC for bail in 2020 Delhi riots cases. The accused submitted that two co-accused, including Tasleem Ahmed, were granted bail by SC on the grou-nd that determination of the issues by the larger bench would take time.

Article Title: Centre eases immigration rules for Pakistani, Afghan minorities and other foreign nationals
Article Text:
The order also streamlines travel and identification protocols for the citizens of Nepal and Bhutan.

NEW DELHI: The Union home ministry has relaxed passport and visa requirements for several categories of foreign nationals residing in India, including Pakistani citizens who entered prior to December 31, 2009 with the intention to permanently reside in India but could not renew their Pakistani passport due to non-possession of computerised nationality identity card issued by Pakistan government.Other categories of foreign nationals for whom passport and visa rules have been eased as part of the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) (Amendment) ORder, 2026, include citizens of Pakistan, Afghanistan and Pakistan belonging to their religious minorities; Sri Lankan Tamil refugees and Tibetans.The order also streamlines travel and identification protocols for the citizens of Nepal and Bhutan, allowing them to enter or exit India by producing any one of the documents specified in the visa manual; However, in case they are entering or exiting India from or to a place other than Nepal or Bhutan, they must in possession of a valid passport. Nepal and Bhutan citizens who have embarked at or transited through China Macau, Hong Kong or Pakistan, must be in possession of both a valid passport and valid visa.The requirement of a valid passport and visa would also not apply to a male member of the Muslim community, being originally an Indian citizen, who went to Pakistan after partition between August 15, 1947 and Dec 31, 1965 leaving behind family in India and returned to India on or before Dec 31, 2009, and settled in Keralam on a valid Pakistani passport but which has since expired or been lost.However, such a person should not have married or acquired immoveable property while in Pakistan; ,while going to Pakistan, left behind family members who are Indian citizens; shall not return to Pakistan; and should not have any adverse report from the police or security agencies.A citizen of India entering into India from Nepal or Bhutan or departing from India to Nepal or Bhutan by land or air shall produce before the immigration officer one of the documents specified in the visa manual to establish their identity, though this exemption would not be applicable if departing to or returning from countries other than Nepal or Bhutan through the Indo-Nepal or Indo-Bhutan border of by air. In all such cases, a valid passport will be required and the exit and entry into India shall be only through the designated immigration points.The provisions in the Act and rules with regard to requirement of valid passport or other valid travel document and valid visa for entry into, stay in and exit from India, shall also not apply for a member of naval, military or air forces of India, entering into or exiting from India on duty and members of the family of any such person when accompanying him on a government transport; registered Sri Lankan Tamil nationals who have taken shelter in India up to Jan 9, 2015; as well as the foreign crew of foreign military vessels coming for repairs in India who are granted military ship repair permits by the immigration officer, provided they hold their military identification documents.Exempted categories include a Tibetan who has entered India after 1959 but before May 30,, 2003 on an entry permit issued by the Embassy of India in Kathmandu; or who entered after May 30, 2003, on the special entry permit issued through the designated immigration post on the Indo-Nepal border and a certificate of registration was issued by the registration officer concerned.Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Christian, Jain and Parsi citizens of Pakistan who entered India before Dec 31, 2024, fearing religious persecution in their home country, without valid documents including passport or other travel documents; or with valid documents including passport that has since expired, would also get relief under the amended Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) order. However, such a person shall be required to obtain an appropriate category of visa after their entry into India, for continued stay.Also exempt now from requirement of a valid passport and visa are persons of Indian origin who subsequently acquired the citizenship of Malaysia or Singapore and returned to India on or before Dec 31, 2009 on a valid passport issued by either of those countries, which has since expired and is not being renewed by those countries because such person does not meet the conditions specified by those countries. Such persons must have documentary proof that they are a person of Indian origin.
Article Summary: The order also streamlines travel and identification protocols for the citizens of Nepal and Bhutan. Pakistani citizens who entered prior to December 31, 2009 could not renew their Pakistani passport due to non-possession of computerised nationality identity card. Other categories of foreign nationals for whom passport and visa rules have been eased include citizens of Pakistan, Afghanistan and Pakistan belonging to their religious minorities.

Article Title: Delhi records 'very poor' air quality on Diwali, 19 monitoring stations report severe AQI
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Delhi's Air Quality Index stood at 371, in the 'very poor' category, on Sunday evening as people stepped out to celebrate DiwaliThe national capital witnessed a further deterioration in air quality as firecracker emissions added to the existing pollution burden. Several residents took to social media platform X to report a smoky smell and hazy conditions in different parts of the city, with some also complaining of reduced visibility.Data from 59 air quality monitoring stations across Delhi painted a grim picture. At 7 pm, 19 stations had recorded 'severe' air quality, while 33 were in the 'very poor' category. The remaining seven stations reported 'poor' air quality.Jahangirpuri emerged as the most polluted location, recording an AQI of 460, placing it firmly in the 'severe' category.Delhi's average AQI for the day was 376, up from 369 on Saturday, indicating a worsening pollution situation ahead of the festival's peak celebrations.The deterioration is expected to continue, with the Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS) forecasting that the city's air quality could slip into the 'severe' category from November 9 and remain there for the next few days.The spike comes as multiple sources of pollution are converging.Firecracker emissions, vehicular exhaust and stubble burning in neighbouring states are expected to compound the problem, while unfavourable weather conditions could prevent pollutants from dispersing.The EWS has flagged poor ventilation conditions as a major concern. A ventilation index below 6,000 square metres per second, along with average wind speeds of less than 10 kilometres per hour, is considered unfavourable for the dispersal of pollutants.PM2.5 remained the dominant pollutant in Delhi on Sunday, with firecracker emissions adding to the concentration of fine particulate matter in the air.According to the Decision Support System (DSS) for Delhi, the transport sector was expected to account for the largest share of the city's pollution load on Sunday, contributing 19 per cent.The contribution from stubble burning was estimated at 3.5 per cent on Sunday and is projected to decline slightly to around 2.99 per cent on Monday.
Article Summary: Jahangirpuri emerged as the most polluted location, recording an AQI of 460. The average AQI for the day was 376, up from 369 on Saturday. Firecracker emissions, vehicular exhaust and stubble burning in neighbouring states are expected to compound the problem.

Article Title: When the smoke settles, what remains? The unseen health and environmental risks
Article Text:
The science of festive pollution and its impact on our everyday lives. (Representative AI image)

Festive celebrations leave behind plastic waste, chemical residues and firecracker debris, polluting our air, water and soil.

Diwali and the science of air pollution

PM2.5 particles penetrate deep into the lungs, trigger inflammation and pose respiratory and cardiovascular health risks.

Beyond the lungs: How festive pollution affects multiple organs

Festive activities release a mix of chemicals, particulate matter and plastic waste, polluting air, water and soil.

Can a few hours of festive pollution cause lasting health problems?

Festive pollutants spread through air, water and soil, entering the food chain and threatening human health and ecosystems.

The environmental footprint of celebrations

Noise pollution: The impact beyond what we can see

The hidden burden of electricity consumption and festive shopping

Festive noise from firecrackers and loud music can damage hearing, disrupt sleep, trigger stress and affect heart health.

Why the effects can last beyond the festivities

Can celebrations become more environmentally responsible?

NEW DELHI: Festivals in India bring people together through lights, colours, music, food and community celebrations. From bursting firecrackers and decorating homes to playing with colours, organising processions and gathering along riverbanks, festivities are an integral part of the country's social and cultural life. But as celebrations grow in scale, so does their environmental footprint.The pollution generated during festivals is often discussed in isolation, particularly when air quality deteriorates after Diwali. However, the environmental impact of celebrations goes much further. Firecrackers release particulate matter into the atmosphere, synthetic colours can introduce chemicals into water bodies, large gatherings generate plastic waste, and loud music and fireworks contribute to noise pollution.These effects are not confined to a particular festival or community. Across different celebrations, the use of disposable materials, increased consumption, transportation, decorative lighting and improper waste disposal can put additional pressure on the environment.The consequences can extend beyond the days of festivities, affecting public health, urban sanitation, water quality and local ecosystems.In cities already struggling with vehicle emissions, industrial pollution, construction dust and untreated waste, the additional burden can make environmental management more challenging.So, what happens to the environment when millions of people celebrate simultaneously, and how do these activities affect our everyday lives?Diwali is among the occasions when the relationship between celebrations and air pollution becomes particularly visible. Firecrackers release a mixture of gases, suspended particles and chemical compounds into the atmosphere. Their emissions include particulate matter such as PM2.5 and PM10, sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides. Depending on their composition, fireworks can also release metallic compounds, including barium and aluminium.The concern is particularly around PM2.5, particles measuring 2.5 micrometres or less. These particles are small enough to penetrate deep into the lungs, reaching the alveoli, the tiny air sacs where oxygen enters the bloodstream. Some components of particulate pollution can also enter the bloodstream and trigger inflammation.Dr Abhishek Agrawal, Medical Officer at a government hospital, explains how exposure to firecracker emissions can affect respiratory health."During festivals like Diwali, the concentration of pollutants in the air can increase due to firecracker emissions. People inhale these pollutants, particularly fine particulate matter, which can enter deep into the lungs and cause irritation and inflammation of the respiratory tract. We often see people complaining of coughing, throat irritation, breathlessness and worsening respiratory symptoms during periods of poor air quality. "The impact is not uniform across the population. Children, elderly people and individuals with pre-existing respiratory conditions are particularly vulnerable to sudden changes in air quality."Children, elderly people and individuals suffering from asthma, COPD or other respiratory conditions are particularly vulnerable. Their respiratory systems may not be able to cope with sudden exposure to high levels of pollution. Even people who do not have a pre-existing respiratory illness can experience discomfort, especially when pollution levels remain elevated for several hours," Agrawal said.The problem can also continue after the celebrations end. During the post-monsoon period, low wind speeds, atmospheric stability and temperature inversions can prevent pollutants from dispersing quickly. When firecracker emissions combine with existing sources such as vehicle exhaust, industrial emissions and construction dust, pollution levels can remain elevated."The effects of pollution do not necessarily disappear once the firecrackers stop. Fine particles can remain suspended in the atmosphere, depending on weather conditions. People may continue experiencing coughing, throat irritation, wheezing and breathing difficulties in the following days. Those with existing respiratory conditions should be especially cautious," Agrawal added.Air pollution is not merely a respiratory concern. Exposure to particulate matter, chemical emissions and excessive noise can affect several organs, including the heart, brain and nervous system.While the lungs are the first point of contact for inhaled pollutants, fine particles can trigger inflammatory responses that affect other parts of the body. Air pollution has been associated with increased blood pressure, disturbances in heart rhythm and a higher risk of cardiovascular complications, particularly among people with existing heart conditions."The impact of festive pollution is not limited to the lungs. Fine particulate matter, particularly PM2.5, can penetrate deep into the alveoli and trigger oxidative stress and inflammation. This can lead to coughing, wheezing, breathlessness and asthma attacks. Air pollution can also increase blood pressure, disturb heart rhythms and trigger cardiovascular complications, including heart attacks, in vulnerable individuals," Agrawal explained.The brain and nervous system can also be affected. Exposure to polluted air and excessive noise can contribute to headaches, dizziness, stress and sleep disturbances. Prolonged exposure to air pollution has also been associated with adverse effects on cognitive health.Chemical exposure presents another concern. Certain toxic metals and chemical residues released by fireworks and other festive materials can pose risks to organs such as the kidneys and liver, depending on the substance, concentration and duration of exposure.Noise pollution adds another dimension to the health burden. Sudden, high-intensity sounds from firecrackers can cause tinnitus, temporary hearing discomfort and, at sufficiently high exposure levels, permanent hearing damage.One of the common misconceptions about festive pollution is that its effects are limited to the duration of celebrations. However, even short-term exposure to high concentrations of pollutants can trigger health complications, particularly among vulnerable individuals.People with asthma may experience sudden attacks, while those with existing respiratory or cardiovascular conditions may develop breathing difficulties or other complications. Repeated exposure over time can increase the risk of chronic health problems."Even a few hours of exposure to high levels of pollution can trigger asthma attacks, breathing difficulties and cardiovascular complications in vulnerable individuals. Repeated exposure increases the risk of long-term health problems. The duration of symptoms varies depending on the level of exposure and the person's health. Some people may recover within a few hours, while others may continue experiencing symptoms for several days," Agrawal said.The effects can also be reflected in healthcare demand. Indian studies examining air pollution during and after Diwali have reported increases in respiratory complaints, hospital visits and admissions, particularly involving asthma exacerbations and breathing difficulties."Studies in India have reported an increase in respiratory hospital visits and admissions following Diwali, particularly involving asthma attacks, breathing difficulties and other respiratory complaints. Hospitals and healthcare facilities also deal with cases involving burns, eye injuries and hearing-related problems during festive periods," Agrawal said.While air pollution receives considerable attention, other forms of environmental degradation often go unnoticed during festivals.The use of synthetic colours during celebrations, for instance, can create problems for water bodies and soil. Some commercially available colours may contain chemical compounds and heavy metals that can cause skin irritation, allergic reactions and eye problems. When washed away, these substances can enter drainage systems and eventually reach rivers, lakes and other water bodies.Similarly, religious offerings, flowers, plastic packaging and decorative materials discarded during large gatherings can add to water and land pollution. Idol immersion activities involving plaster of Paris, synthetic paints and non-biodegradable decorations can further increase the waste entering lakes and rivers.The consequences are particularly concerning in urban areas where water bodies are already under pressure from untreated sewage, industrial discharge and solid waste. Additional festive waste can worsen existing contamination and affect aquatic ecosystems.Large public celebrations and processions also generate considerable quantities of disposable plates, plastic bottles, food packaging and other materials. When waste is not segregated or collected properly, it can clog drains, accumulate in public spaces and eventually enter nearby water bodies.The problem does not end with the celebrations. Municipal sanitation workers are often left to clear large quantities of discarded materials, firecracker remnants, food waste and plastic packaging. Improper disposal and open burning of collected waste can further contribute to local pollution.Another dimension of festive pollution is noise, which can affect people even when there is no visible deterioration in air quality.Firecrackers, loudspeakers, musical processions and public celebrations can expose residential neighbourhoods to excessive sound levels. Sudden explosions and prolonged exposure to loud music can interfere with sleep, concentration and everyday routines.Repeated exposure to excessive noise can also contribute to stress, anxiety and hearing-related problems. People with cardiovascular conditions, infants, elderly residents and patients recovering from illnesses may be particularly affected by disturbances during late-night celebrations.The impact extends to animals and urban wildlife. Pets can experience distress due to sudden loud noises, while birds and other species may alter their movement and behaviour in response to repeated disturbances.The World Health Organization has associated excessive environmental noise with sleep disturbance, hearing impairment and cardiovascular health risks. This makes noise pollution an important public health concern rather than merely an inconvenience during celebrations.Modern celebrations also involve a considerable increase in consumption. Decorative lighting across homes, markets and commercial establishments increases electricity demand, while shopping, gift packaging, food deliveries and travel add to energy use and waste generation.Although LED lights consume less electricity than conventional lighting, their widespread use across residential and commercial areas can still contribute to higher cumulative demand.Excessive artificial lighting also contributes to light pollution, which can interfere with the natural day-night cycles of birds, insects and other wildlife. For nocturnal species, artificial illumination can affect navigation, feeding and other behavioural patterns.The growing use of plastic decorations, disposable utensils, thermocol, synthetic materials and packaging creates another challenge. Much of this waste is used for a limited period before being discarded, adding to the burden on already stretched municipal waste-management systems.These individual activities may appear relatively small, but their combined impact across densely populated cities can be considerable.One of the reasons festive pollution becomes a concern is that the environmental impact does not always end when celebrations stop.Airborne particles can remain suspended depending on weather conditions, while chemical residues and improperly disposed materials can continue affecting soil and water quality. Waste accumulated in drainage systems can also create problems during subsequent rainfall.The extent of pollution depends on several factors, including the scale of celebrations, the materials used, local environmental conditions and the efficiency of waste collection and disposal.It is also important to distinguish between pollution generated during festivals and the wider pollution crisis. Festivals are not the sole reason behind deteriorating air or water quality. Instead, they can add concentrated emissions and waste to an environment already dealing with multiple sources of contamination.This cumulative impact also raises questions about environmental inequality. A person celebrating indoors may have limited exposure to pollution, while a street vendor, traffic policeman, delivery worker or sanitation worker may remain exposed for several hours. Similarly, children and people with existing health conditions may face greater health risks than others.Reducing festive pollution does not mean giving up celebrations. It requires greater awareness of how everyday choices during these occasions affect the environment.Using natural colours, opting for traditional clay idols, avoiding single-use plastics, segregating waste and ensuring that religious offerings are disposed of responsibly can help reduce the burden on water bodies and public spaces. Community celebrations, designated immersion facilities and better waste collection can also improve environmental management.Individual precautions are equally important, particularly during periods of poor air quality. Agrawal recommends avoiding areas with heavy firecracker smoke, limiting outdoor activities when pollution levels are high and taking measures to reduce indoor exposure."People should avoid unnecessary outdoor activities when air quality is poor, particularly during early morning and late evening hours if pollution levels are elevated. Patients with asthma should follow their prescribed medication and treatment plans. Children and elderly people should limit exposure to smoke and avoid areas where firecrackers are being burst."He also recommends wearing a well-fitted N95 mask when outdoor exposure to particulate pollution cannot be avoided, keeping windows closed during periods of heavy pollution and using HEPA air purifiers indoors, if available.Outdoor exercise should be avoided when pollution levels are high. Firecracker residues should be cleaned using damp methods rather than dry sweeping, which can resuspend particles in the air.People experiencing persistent breathlessness, wheezing or chest pain should seek medical attention rather than dismissing the symptoms as temporary festive discomfort.Ultimately, the environmental cost of celebrations cannot be measured only by the pollution recorded on a particular day. It must also account for the waste left behind, the pressure on natural resources and the health implications for people who continue to live and work in these surroundings.Festivals are an important part of India's cultural and social fabric. The challenge is to ensure that the joy of celebrations does not come at the cost of the air people breathe, the water they depend on and the environment they share.
Article Summary: Festive activities release a mix of chemicals, particulate matter and plastic waste. PM2.5 particles penetrate deep into the lungs, trigger inflammation and pose respiratory and cardiovascular health risks. Children, elderly people and individuals with pre-existing respiratory conditions are particularly vulnerable to sudden changes in air quality.

Article Title: 3 Nigerian nationals arrested in Delhi for staying without valid documents
Article Text:
Three Nigerian nationals arrested in Delhi for overstaying without valid documents and sent to a detention centre

NEW DELHI: Three Nigerian nationals were arrested by the Delhi Police for allegedly staying in India without valid documents and subsequently sent to a detention centre, news agency PTI reported citing officials on Sunday.Following their arrest, they were produced before the foreigners regional registration office (FRRO) and later sent to Sewa Sadan detention centre in Lampur, officials said.The arrests were made on October 31 during a verification drive in southwest Delhi's Dwarka.The three men allegedly failed to produce documents authorising their stay in the country.Police identified the accused as Bartholomew Uwaebuka Iloegbunem, Konan Okocha alias Konan Brice Kousaai and Ndubuisi Charles Nwabufor.

Article Title: Rajasthan's local poll rolls have 30 lakh more voters than EC's final SIR list: Activist
Article Text:
In Rajasthan, a troubling disparity has emerged regarding the electoral rolls for local body elections, with the state election commission clinging to a voter list that dates back to January 2025.

Activist questions use of outdated voter lists

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nearly 30 lakh voters listed in electoral rolls used for local body elections in Rajasthan are absent from the election commission's final voter list following the Special intensive revision (SIR) exercise, a civil rights activist has alleged.According to news agency PTI, the discrepancy reportedly exists between the election commission's final SIR electoral roll and the voter lists maintained by the Rajasthan state election commission (SEC) for urban local body and panchayat elections.The SEC has attributed the difference to its continued use of the pre-SIR electoral roll, explaining that preparations for local elections had started well before the revision exercise was completed.According to Rajasthan's final SIR electoral roll, published in February 2026, the state's electorate declined from 5.47 crore to 5.15 crore. The revision resulted in the deletion of 44.28 lakh names and the addition of 12.91 lakh new voters.However, the SEC's electoral rolls covering the same 199 Assembly constituencies continued to carry approximately 5.45 crore names, creating a difference of nearly 30 lakh voters.SEC secretary Rajesh Verma said the commission had adopted the Election Commission's pre-SIR electoral roll, which was last updated on January 1, 2025, as the basis for preparing voter lists for local elections.He added that the SEC traditionally relies on election commission electoral rolls updated through the annual special summary revision process for local body polls.Chief electoral officer Naveen Mahajan also confirmed that the SEC had used the pre-SIR list. He said no objections had been received in Rajasthan against the final SIR electoral roll.Nikhil Dey, rights activist and founder of the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan, questioned the SEC's decision to continue using the older electoral roll despite the availability of the revised list.Dey argued that electoral rolls undergo regular updates and that the state election commission could have adopted the election commission's final SIR list instead.He also sought clarification on why the SEC considered its older voter list more reliable than the election commission's final version.Raising concerns over the apparent inconsistency, Dey questioned how booth-level officers could mark individuals as deceased in one electoral roll while their names continued to appear in another.A comparative analysis conducted by Dey found that 26.63 lakh voters whose names were removed during the SIR exercise were still listed in the SEC's 2026 electoral rolls for urban local body and panchayat elections.
Article Summary: Activist questions use of outdated voter lists in Rajasthan. State election commission clinging to a voter list that dates back to January 2025. Nearly 30 lakh voters listed in electoral rolls used for local body elections are absent from the election commission's final voter list following the Special intensive revision (SIR) exercise.

Article Title: 'Engines failing': DKS accuses Centre of 'cover up' amid ethanol blending row
Article Text:
Calling the issue a major concern for the country, the chief minister alleged that cheaper ethanol was being mixed with petrol to increase profits

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Sunday targeted the Centre over allegations of excessive ethanol blending in petrol, claiming that thousands of vehicles were experiencing problems, including repeated engine failures and reduced mileage. He said the state government had collected samples from 67 locations and was investigating complaints about ethanol levels exceeding the prescribed limit."Engines are stopping repeatedly, and mileage has decreased," Shivakumar said, adding that around 30% of the investigation had been completed. He said the state government had already informed the Centre about the locations and that its findings would be made public."We have conducted an investigation first. 30% [of the work] is complete. Tomorrow, our Minister will officially hold a press conference and give all details. The government cannot cover it up," he said, as quoted by news agency ANI.Shivakumar alleged that excessive ethanol mixing was taking place at petrol pumps rather than during the supply process. "We have checked, and the mixing is happening at the petrol bunks.Where it is being distributed, mixing is happening there. We have all the documents," he said.Calling the issue a major concern for the country, the chief minister alleged that cheaper ethanol was being mixed with petrol to increase profits. "Because it is available at a lower price, they are mixing it to make a profit. We condemn this. It is dangerous. People need to be made aware and protected," he added.The remarks come amid a dispute between the Karnataka government and public sector oil marketing companies over allegations that petrol sold at some outlets in the state contained ethanol levels significantly higher than the prescribed 20% limit.Karnataka food, civil supplies, consumer affairs and legal metrology minister Rizwan Arshad had earlier said tests on samples collected from seven locations, including Bengaluru, Kolar, Chikkaballapura, Ramanagara, Mangaluru and Tumakuru, had recorded ethanol levels as high as 31.2%.However, Indian Oil Corporation Limited, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited rejected the allegations in a joint statement on Friday. The companies maintained that petrol supplied by them across the country, including Karnataka, complied with the Bureau of Indian Standards specification for E20 fuel.They also questioned the sampling procedure and testing methodology used in the state government's October 2026 exercise, arguing that the findings were based on third-party laboratory certificates that did not follow the prescribed statutory and technical procedures.
Article Summary: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar targeted the Centre over allegations of excessive ethanol blending in petrol. He claimed that thousands of vehicles were experiencing problems, including repeated engine failures and reduced mileage. The remarks come amid a dispute between the Karnataka government and public sector oil marketing companies.

NEW DELHI: Contributions received by the Congress in excess of Rs 20,000 totalled Rs 130.7 crore in 2025-26, which is barely one-fourth of its Rs 517.4 crore donation receipts in 2024-25.As per the 2025-26 contribution report of the Congress filed with EC, Prudent Electoral Trust contributed 19% of Congress's total donation kitty in the relevant year. In 2024-25, Prudent had accounted for 41.8% of contributions received by Congress.Prudent is the only electoral trust through which donations, largely corporate, were routed to Congress last year. At Rs 25 crore, the trust's contributions to the party, however, were only 11.5% of the Rs 216 crore funds it had channelled to the party in 2024-25.The steep 75% decline in Congress's total contributions in excess of Rs 20,000, compared with 2024-25, could be due to several factors. Given that 2024-25 was the general election year, a marked rise (84% as compared to 2023-24) in contributions to the main opposition party was on expected lines. What is interesting though is that the Rs 130.7 crore contribution receipts in 2025-26 are nearly 53% less than the amount it had received even in 2023-24.The steep decline was witnessed despite 2025-26 being the year of Bihar assembly elections and the run-up to elections in Assam, Keralam, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry held in April 2026.The Congress audit report for 2025-26, which is not available yet, will throw light on the party's other sources of funding. Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Who is Alice Huang? Chinese businesswoman at centre of Nvidia spy scandal
Article Text:
The allegations have prompted Nvidia's board to launch an independent investigation

From television reporter to a top executive at Megaspeed

Intelligence operation and Megaspeed's China links

Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman accused by US intelligence agencies of working for Beijing, has emerged at the centre of a major controversy involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. According to a report by The New York Times, China's Ministry of State Security recruited Alice Huang to gather intelligence on the chipmaker's chief executive and potentially influence the company's decisions on advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chip sales to China.The allegations have prompted Nvidia's board to launch an independent investigation after reports that Jensen Huang, 63, had developed a close relationship with the businesswoman. The Nvidia chief has separately admitted to being unfaithful to his wife and apologised to his family and colleagues. However, the company has maintained that it has no reason to believe its trade secrets or US national security were compromised.Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese citizen who previously worked as a television reporter in China before moving into the technology and business sector. She eventually became a senior executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a data centre company that provides AI computing infrastructure to businesses, including major Chinese technology firms.According to The New York Times, Megaspeed began making multibillion-dollar purchases of advanced Nvidia chips around 2024. The company reportedly bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia processors over two years, making it one of the chipmaker's biggest customers in Southeast Asia.Huang is also understood to have developed connections with senior executives across the AI chip industry. She attended technology conferences and private business dinners and had professional links with leaders at companies involved in assembling Nvidia-powered supercomputers.The New York Times reported that US intelligence agencies had monitored her communications for at least a year before concluding that she was working for China's Ministry of State Security (MSS). A classified intelligence assessment circulated among senior Trump administration officials reportedly identified her as an asset recruited to collect information on Jensen Huang.US intelligence agencies determined that Alice Huang, pictured drinking whiskey and dining with the tech mogul, was secretly passing information to Beijing, the newspaper reported.The report also said electronic surveillance identified Jensen Huang as one of her contacts. The two are not related.According to the intelligence assessment cited by The New York Times, Beijing's objective was potentially to gain insights into Nvidia's operations and influence its position on allowing China access to advanced AI processors.Megaspeed's business model has also come under scrutiny. The company reportedly built data centres across Southeast Asia and rented computing power to Chinese technology firms, including Alibaba. This arrangement could potentially provide Chinese companies access to advanced Nvidia chips despite US restrictions on direct sales to China.US authorities have also examined whether Megaspeed helped Chinese companies circumvent export restrictions. The New York Times reported that the network of businesses and investors connected to Huang had links to companies in Shanghai and Zhejiang, as well as financial connections to China's military technology establishment.Alice Huang has not publicly responded to the allegations or multiple requests for comment. Megaspeed has said its current leadership takes the claims seriously and has appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation.Nvidia, meanwhile, has defended Jensen Huang's interactions with the businesswoman, describing them as normal customer engagements. A company spokesperson said the CEO regularly meets thousands of customer executives and that such interactions do not involve sensitive trade secrets.
Article Summary: Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen who previously worked as a television reporter in China. She became a senior executive at Megaspeed, a data centre company that provides AI computing infrastructure to businesses, including major Chinese technology firms. US intelligence agencies monitored her communications for at least a year before concluding that she was working for China's Ministry of State Security.

Article Title: A North Dakota woman spent more than $110,000 on purchases for a house she built with her partner on land held by his family trust; after they split, a court rejected her claim for the home's improvem
Article Text:
Proof of spending is not proof of added value

Legal principle of unjust enrichment

End of lengthy multi-year litigation

A North Dakota woman who spent more than $110,000 on building materials and other items for a home on land owned by her longtime partner's family trust cannot get her money back through an unjust enrichment claim, the North Dakota Supreme Court has ruled. The decision, issued on Friday, 6 November 2026, upheld a Grant County District Court ruling that rejected a financial claim filed by Mary Roth. She had sought repayment after her relationship with rancher Gary Meyer ended. The case involved a 10-acre residential property in rural Grant County, North Dakota, where the couple lived and ran a cattle business together. Gary Meyer had lived on the property for decades and believed he owned it. However, the legal ownership belonged to the Jean L. Ehrmantrout Residuary Trust, which was managed by his three sons as co-trustees. After the relationship ended, Roth asked to be repaid for the large number of items and materials she bought to build and improve the home. She also filed an unjust enrichment claim against the trust's beneficiaries, arguing that they had unfairly benefited from her spending.Writing for the unanimous Supreme Court, Justice Jon J. Jensen explained that showing how much money someone spent is not enough to win an unjust enrichment claim under North Dakota law.The court said these claims must focus on the actual financial benefit received by the property owner. They cannot be based only on the money spent by the person who bought the materials or paid for the work. "Receipts and a compilation of purchases show what Mary Roth spent; they do not show the value those purchases added to the property," Justice Jensen wrote in the opinion. Roth provided many receipts and financial records showing that she had spent more than $110,000. However, she did not provide expert evidence or property appraisals showing how much those purchases had actually increased the market value of the land owned by the family trust.Under North Dakota law, a person making an unjust enrichment claim must prove five main things. First, the defendant received a benefit. Second, the person making the claim suffered a financial loss. Third, there must be a clear connection between that benefit and the financial loss. Fourth, there must be no valid reason for the benefit and loss to have occurred. Finally, there must be no other legal remedy available. The Supreme Court noted that the district court had accepted that Roth suffered a financial loss by paying for building materials and supplies for the home. However, there was not enough evidence to work out how much financial benefit the trust had received. The justices rejected the idea that purchase receipts or property listing prices could automatically be used to prove how much a property had gained in value. They said trial judges cannot simply estimate an increase in market value without proper evidence from property valuation experts. The court also referred to its 2018 decision in Tornabeni v. Wold. It repeated the legal principle that a person cannot receive compensation through an equity claim based only on money spent. They must also prove that the property owner received a clear and measurable financial benefit.The ruling on 6 November, marks the third time the dispute between Roth and the Meyer estate has reached the North Dakota Supreme Court. The earlier appeals took place in 2024 and 2025. Chief Justice Lisa Fair McEvers, Justice Jerod E. Tufte, Justice Douglas A. Bahr and Justice Mark A. Friese all agreed with Justice Jensen's opinion. Their decision brings the long-running property dispute to an end. The Supreme Court upheld the Grant County District Court's third amended judgment. This means the property will remain with the family trust, and Roth will not receive the money she sought to recover. The ruling also underscores the importance of proving the actual increase in a property's value when seeking compensation for improvements.
Article Summary: Mary Roth spent more than $110,000 on building materials and other items for a home on land owned by her longtime partner's family trust. Roth asked to be repaid for the large number of items and materials she bought to build and improve the home. She also filed an unjust enrichment claim against the trust's beneficiaries, arguing that they had unfairly benefited from her spending.

Article Title: Meet Jacob, the 14-year-old from England who started selling tomato plants from a small cart and now grows 7,000 plants, with customers ordering from overseas
Article Text:
Meet Jacob, Founder of The Tomato Cart. Image Credit: The Shropshire Seaweed

14-year-old Jacob turned a gardening hobby into The Tomato Cart

From a handful of plants to 7,000 in a greenhouse

Why customers keep returning to his tomato cart

How The Tomato Cart expanded beyond local markets

Jacob's ambition is to encourage more people to grow food

Jacob Mann, 14, from Norwich, England, has turned his love of gardening into a growing business selling tomato plants, growing kits and tomato merchandise. It all started from humble beginnings with a few seedlings and a home-made bicycle trailer, and has grown into The Tomato Cart, growing thousands of plants each year with customers from far and wide, even beyond the UK. Jacob now cultivates up to 7,000 tomato plants to meet demand, with his products attracting buyers as far away as Australia, BBC reports. He started with a family gardening competition during the Covid pandemic.Jacob's interest in growing plants developed during the pandemic, when his family decided to turn their vegetable patch into a friendly competition. While the other plots struggled, his continued to flourish, giving him an early indication that gardening was something he enjoyed and could do well.In a case study published by The Shropshire Seaweed Company, Jacob explained that the experience encouraged him to take growing more seriously. He subsequently began thinking about establishing his own garden centre one day, selling plants he had raised himself.The opportunity to start earning money came a few years later. When his brother began making money through a paper round, Jacob also wanted to earn independently.Rather than simply taking up a conventional job, he decided to build something around his interests.Tomatoes became his starting point because they were enjoyable to grow and could eventually be eaten. He collected a greenhouse found through Freecycle with his father just two days before his 13th birthday in December 2024.He then saved his pocket money to purchase an old trailer base through Gumtree. Together with his father, he turned it into a specially designed cart that could be attached to a bicycle and taken to local markets and car boot sales.The business became The Tomato Cart, allowing Jacob to sell plants directly to customers around Norwich.The early business was modest, but Jacob's growing experience and customer interest helped it expand. BBC reported in March 2026 that he had initially sold approximately 14 plants before demand increased significantly.He had built up a greenhouse containing as many as 7,000 plants. Managing that volume requires considerable work, particularly because tomato plants need regular attention and the growing season is relatively short.He grows thousands of plants each year alongside his school work, the Shropshire Seaweed Company said. He waters plants before school, and his parents help to ensure that his business obligations do not interfere with his education.Weather has also been a considerable challenge. Jacob told the company that unpredictable British conditions, from freezing nights to heatwaves, made growing large numbers of plants difficult. Before installing greenhouse heaters, he sometimes had to bring plants indoors overnight to protect them from the cold.His early days of selling at markets was another obstacle. At first Jacob worried people might not take him seriously because he was so young. He was uncomfortable at first explaining his products to people and appearing in social media videos but through customer support, he slowly got more confident.For Jacob, selling plants is not simply about making money. One of the most rewarding parts of the business is hearing from customers who have successfully grown tomatoes using his plants.He enjoys seeing photographs of customers' first harvests and hearing how their plants have developed. This feedback makes the time spent sowing seeds, watering plants and preparing them for sale worthwhile.His experience and growing knowledge also allow him to help customers select varieties suited to their gardens. With support and advice from Nick at JustSeed, he has developed a selection ranging from familiar favourites to less common tomato varieties.The business has also received attention beyond local markets. According to the Shropshire Seaweed Company, Jacob has appeared on podcasts, in local newspapers and on radio programmes. He also attended the RHS Sandringham Flower Show, where he met gardening personalities Rekha Mistry, Ade Sellars and Alan Titchmarsh.As the number of plants Jacob grows increased, he began looking for ways to reach customers outside Norwich. His business now operates through several channels, including markets, online sales and his own website.The Tomato Cart's official website describes Jacob as a Norwich-area teenager selling tomato plants through a specially designed bicycle trailer. It also advertises home growing kits through Etsy, alongside local delivery and pre-orders.The expansion has helped him address a problem common to seasonal plant businesses. Tomato plants are mainly sold during a limited period of the year, leaving fewer opportunities to generate income during the colder months.Jacob responded by developing products that customers could purchase beyond the main planting season. These include home growing kits, which contain seeds, compost, plant labels, pots and instructions written by him.The website also features a pizza-growing kit containing San Marzano tomato, basil and oregano seeds. The idea allows customers to grow ingredients associated with pizza from their own homes, including on a windowsill before moving the plants outdoors.Another unique addition is Adopt a Tomato, a collection of crocheted tomato keyrings sold with adoption cards. The products give the business a playful identity while allowing Jacob to continue selling something when his greenhouse plants are not ready for customers.BBC reported that his merchandise has attracted international interest, with a customer in Australia purchasing a crocheted tomato mascot. The buyer was around 10,000 miles away, illustrating how a small business operating from Norwich can reach people well beyond its local community.He believes growing tomatoes, herbs or vegetables can help people understand where their food comes from and appreciate the process of producing it. Watching a plant develop from a seed into something edible is central to what he wants customers to experience.His business has also developed a partnership with The Shropshire Seaweed Company, whose organic liquid seaweed fertiliser he already used while growing plants.
Article Summary: Jacob Mann, 14, from Norwich, England, has turned his love of gardening into a growing business selling tomato plants, growing kits and tomato merchandise.
