It all started with a few seedlings and a home-made bicycle trailer, and has grown into The Tomato Cart. Jacob now cultivates up to 7,000 tomato plants to meet demand, with his products attracting buyers as far away as Australia.

Article Title: In 2015, Tiger Woods invested in Full Swing, a golf-simulator maker; in July 2026 Versant agreed to buy it for $530 million, and his reported 2% stake could be worth up to $10.6 million
Article Text:
Tiger Woods at 2020 PNC Championship. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Versant announced the complete purchase of Full Swing on August 3, 2026

Wood’s stake is an estimate based on one unnamed source

Simulator users grew from 3.8 million in 2015 to 8.1 million in 2024

.

A Full Swing golf simulator. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

70% of facilities with simulators report a positive financial impact

Tiger Woods invested in the golf simulator manufacturer Full Swing in 2015. On July 6, 2026, Versant Media Group agreed to acquire the company for $530 million, subject to customary adjustments, according to its Form 8-K filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. As per Front Office Sports, Woods owns shares worth 1% to 2%. Considering that a 2% share would amount to around $10.6 million at the valuation price, it is clear that this figure is just an approximation.Versant’s Media Group’s press release names Bruin Capital, the majority owner and a group of minority investors as the sellers. Bruin paid $160 million for Full Swing in 2021, as Front Office Sports noted, so the $530 million sale is roughly three times that figure five years later. Versant, having spun off from Comcast and owning Golf Channel, made this announcement on August 3, 2026. Its second-quarter results , filed on August 6, also list the acquisition as completed after the quarter ended.Woods has been Full Swing brand ambassador since 2015 and Front Office Sports says he has had a significant influence on the company's business direction and product development despite holding a minority stake. Since his stake could be as low as 1%, the $10.6 million is a ceiling rather than a confirmed payout and the final figure could shift with purchase price adjustments and profit-sharing terms.He has had a significant influence on the companies' business direction and product development despite holding a minority stake. Full Swing is the official licensed simulator of the PGA Tour and a technology partner of TGL, the indoor golf league co-founded by Woods and Rory McIlroy. Jordan Spieth and Xander Schauffele are among the athletes associated with the brand.Woods backed Full Swing in 2015; the same year, the National Golf Foundation counted 3,800,000 simulator and screen golf users, according to its 2025 white paper, The Golf Simulator Opportunity It puts the 2024 figure at 8.1 million. The National Golf Foundation’s 2025 report also found that 51% of golf simulator users had not played on a traditional golf course in the previous 12 months, up from 42% a decade earlier. The foundation Research also found that three-quarters of simulator users were likely to return.Golfers listed various reasons why they chose to play indoors. Weather-proofing was mentioned by 59% of golfers and performance improvement by 43%, while 34% mentioned performance analysis.The National Golf Foundation’s study puts US golf participation at a record 47.2 million in 2024, which counts formats like simulators on top of the 28.1 million who played on a course. The study is based on two surveys conducted in November and December 2024. One survey of 354 US golf venues and another one of 569 core golfers, who played at least eight rounds in the past year.As noted above in the NGF report, 70% of facilities with simulators have recorded positive financial effects. According to the same research, 80% of those facilities reached profitability within a year of getting a simulator and 44% saw a positive financial impact within the first month, rather than a full return on the investment. Operators spent an average of $45,000 per bay. Each session cost an average of $55, while customers spent an additional $40 on food and drinks. 6.5% of all US golf facilities had installed simulators at the time of the survey, while another 13% were planning to get simulators in 1 to 2 years. Of those not having simulators, 72% stated space was their constraint and 53% pointed out the cost.
Article Summary: Tiger Woods invested in the golf simulator manufacturer Full Swing in 2015. On July 6, 2026, Versant Media Group agreed to acquire the company for $530 million. As per Front Office Sports, Woods owns shares worth 1% to 2%. 70% of facilities with simulators report a positive financial impact.

Article Title: Inside Tom Brady’s billionaire bunker plans: The Miami waterfront lot that put the seven-time champion next to some of the richest neighbors in America
Article Text:
Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen bought a $17 million lot on Miami’s Indian Creek Island in 2020, planning an eco-friendly home. (Image via Getty)

How Tom Brady ended up on Miami’s Billionaire Bunker

Why the island earned its bunker reputation

What Tom Brady built on the water

Why $150 million bids are only part of the story

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tom Brady paid $17 million for a teardown lot on Miami’s Indian Creek Island in late 2020. Over the next few years he turned it into a finished waterfront estate. The island, nicknamed the Billionaire Bunker, is home to Jared Kushner, Ivanka Trump and Jeff Bezos. In January 2025, Bloomberg reported that bids on Brady’s house had passed $150 million, though no public listing followed. A sale at that level would beat Miami’s single-family record.Tom Brady was still a Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback when the deal came together. Page Six reported in December 2020 that he and then-wife Gisele Bündchen had bought the property at 26 Indian Creek Island Road. The couple were renting Derek Jeter’s Tampa mansion at the time, so the purchase was a quiet bet on life after football.The transaction appears to have happened off market. It went through an LLC tied to Jeff Soffer’s Fontainebleau Development. Soffer is a close friend of Brady and lives next door at number 27. That detail says a lot about how deals work on the island: introductions matter as much as price.The lot covers roughly two acres, with about 200 feet of water frontage, according to reports at the time. The plan from the start was to demolish the existing house and build something new and eco-friendly.Brady retired for good in February 2023, so he did not live there while he played. He bought the place for the years after the game.Indian Creek is a man-made island in Biscayne Bay, and it works more like a private village than a neighborhood. It has an 18-hole golf course and a country club. It also has its own police force and its own mayor. Access is gated and tightly controlled.The neighbors explain the nickname. Kushner and Ivanka Trump reportedly paid more than $30 million for their lot. Billionaire investor Carl Icahn has a home there. Bezos has spent more than $230 million on three properties since 2023, according to Business Insider and Bloomberg.For someone with Brady’s profile, the appeal is easy to read. He spent twenty years being watched. On Indian Creek, the real product is privacy. The price tag mostly pays for the security around the house, not just the house itself.The build was not cheap, and it was not quick. In 2023, The Real Deal reported that Brady had secured a $35 million construction loan for the property. First Republic Bank was the original lender, but it failed, and JPMorgan stepped in to provide the financing. That loan alone suggests the construction bill ran well into eight figures.Renderings from Scott Mitchell Studio, obtained by The Real Deal in September 2023, showed a modern waterfront house. The primary and guest suites each have their own terraces. Later reports described a pickleball court, a basketball court, a custom golf area, an outdoor infinity pool and a boat dock. The mansion was reported complete in 2024.The divorce changed the story around the house. Brady and Bündchen split in 2022, and per their settlement, Brady kept the Indian Creek property. Bündchen moved into her own place in Surfside, bought for $11.5 million. It sits almost directly across the water from his estate. Two homes that were once planned as one family’s future now look at each other across a short stretch of bay.The Bloomberg report in January 2025 said Brady was open to selling and that the house was being shown to a small group of buyers. Bids had reportedly topped $150 million. Bloomberg also noted that those discussions did not guarantee a sale, and Brady’s representatives did not comment.The number looks less strange against the island’s recent market. Ken Griffin set Miami’s previous single-family record in 2022, paying $107 million for a Coconut Grove estate. A vacant 1.84-acre lot on Indian Creek, bought for $27.5 million in 2018, was later on the market for $200 million. Bezos moving in lifted everything around him.Then the ceiling moved again. In March 2026, the Wall Street Journal reported that Mark Zuckerberg had bought an Indian Creek mansion for $170 million, now the largest residential sale in Miami-Dade County. That means a Brady sale at $150 million would no longer take the record. It would still land among the biggest deals the city has seen.For now, the facts are narrower than the headlines. Brady bought a $17 million lot, built a house on it and has been reported to have heard offers far above that. No public sale record has confirmed a deal. The most useful number may be the oldest one: $17 million was what the land cost in 2020, before Bezos, before Zuckerberg, and before the island became a bidding war.
Article Summary: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen bought a $17 million lot on Miami’s Indian Creek Island in 2020, planning an eco-friendly home. Over the next few years he turned it into a finished waterfront estate. The island, nicknamed the Billionaire Bunker, is home to Jared Kushner, Ivanka Trump and Jeff Bezos.

Article Title: Nvidia shares drop after CEO Jensen Huang admits affair with suspected Chinese spy; what it means for company
Article Text:
Huang acknowledged that he had been unfaithful to his wife but did not provide details about the relationship.

Jensen Huang & the 'Chinese spy' scandal

Impact on Nvidia and its shares

Nvidia shares declined in after-hours trading on Monday following the announcement of an internal investigation to find out if the company’s chief executive Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The investigation has raised questions about Jensen Huang’s future at the AI chipmaker which is among the most valuable listed companies in the world.Announced on Sunday, the investigation has drawn attention to Huang's position at Nvidia, the world's most valuable chipmaker. His future is also under scrutiny because of his prominent role as one of the leading salesmen of the artificial intelligence boom.Jensen Huang, 63, has headed Nvidia since he established the company in 1993 alongside Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. His long tenure makes him one of Silicon Valley's longest-serving chief executives among company founders.Born in Taiwan and brought up in the US, Huang emerged as a key figure in the artificial intelligence revolution. He steered Nvidia from its original business of manufacturing graphics chips for video games to becoming the world's leading supplier of AI processors.The company launched the internal inquiry following a media report alleging that Huang had a close association with a Chinese businesswoman who had allegedly shared information with Beijing.In a message to Nvidia employees, Huang acknowledged that he had been unfaithful to his wife but did not provide details about the relationship.The New York Times reported last month that Huang had been involved in a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed who is not related to him. US authorities investigated Alice Huang and concluded that she was an asset of Chinese intelligence.Megaspeed's website identifies the company as an Nvidia Cloud Partner in the Asia-Pacific region. It also lists Nvidia's GB200 NVL72 and HGX H100 chips among the products it offers.The developments also had repercussions in South Korea. Madison Huang, Jensen Huang's daughter and an Nvidia executive, called off a scheduled visit to Seoul for an Nvidia conference due to begin on Monday, according to companies that had been due to meet her.Madison Huang had been scheduled to visit South Korean artificial intelligence startup Rebellions and participate in a question-and-answer session with Kakao Mobility. Rebellions said both engagements had been called off because of "unavoidable internal circumstances at Nvidia."South Korean media reported that Nvidia AI Day Seoul, a two-day conference expected to attract around 2,000 participants, would go ahead as scheduled. The event is set to focus on physical AI, agentic AI and infrastructure. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.According to a Reuters report, trading in perpetual futures on the Hyperliquid exchange, along with after-hours share transactions on the Blue Ocean system, indicated that Nvidia shares were changing hands at around $178.60. This is a decline of more than 4% from the stock's closing price of $186.64 on the Nasdaq on Friday.Nvidia's chip technology has played a central role in several major shifts in the technology industry, spanning video gaming, autonomous vehicles, cloud computing and artificial intelligence.Huang's early decision to invest in AI proved significant. By the time ChatGPT was launched in late 2022, Nvidia's processors were already central to the computing infrastructure needed to meet the rapidly growing demand for AI applications.The company's market value has since climbed sharply, making it one of the world's most valuable businesses and an essential supplier to leading technology companies. Nvidia's valuation rose from $420 billion in late 2022 to $4.5 trillion as of November 6."The market's probably telling you now this does no favours ⁠to the stock whatsoever in a time when there's a lot of conjecture as to the build out of data centres," Chris Weston, head of research at brokerage Pepperstone in Melbourne told Reuters.However, Weston said he did not expect Huang, whom he described as the "godfather of AI", to be replaced."If we genuinely thought he was going to step down ... the stock would be down — it would be an absolute bloodbath, to be honest,” he said.The scrutiny of Huang's relationship with Alice Huang has emerged at a sensitive point for Nvidia. Investors are already questioning whether the AI boom that fuelled the company's extraordinary growth can be sustained. The board's investigation has added another layer of uncertainty by raising questions about the future of the executive most closely linked to Nvidia's success.The issue has also drawn attention from senior Republicans in the US House of Representatives, who have sought briefings from Huang following The New York Times report, pointing to concerns over national security.Nvidia has maintained that its board has "no reason to believe" that US national security or company secrets were compromised. However, an independent committee of directors will examine all the information available as part of its review.Analysts cautioned that an extended investigation or internal review could affect Nvidia's investment decisions and product launches, potentially creating wider repercussions for the semiconductor industry.Ryu Young-ho, a senior analyst at NH Investment & Securities, said competitors such as Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) could receive increased attention in the near term. This could also bring Samsung into greater focus because of its close business ties ⁠with AMD.However, Ryu said Nvidia's products would be difficult to replace, which could limit the overall impact of the developments. He added that shipments to China might face further delays, depending on how the situation unfolded.South Korea's deputy science minister said on Monday that the government did not expect any disruption to deliveries of Nvidia graphics processing units covered by existing contracts, despite the challenges currently confronting the company.Shares of Nvidia's major Asian chip suppliers recovered on Monday following last week's selloff in AI-related stocks. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) rose 6.5%, while Samsung Electronics gained 2.9% and SK Hynix advanced 4.7%.Several prominent personalities also commented on Huang's admission. Billionaire investor Bill Ackman, who founded Pershing Square Capital Management, described the Nvidia chief executive as an "incredible human" in a post on X. However, he added that ‌if "indeed this is ⁠more than an affair, then it is obviously a real problem.""I am hoping for a simple affair, not a risk to our national security," he added.Tesla CEO Elon Musk responded with "I agree" to a post by Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire. Maguire had said Huang "did something incredibly dumb" that was "bad for America", while also maintaining that "Jensen is irreplaceable for America's AI leadership".US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that he had not discussed the allegations with Huang. He nevertheless described the Nvidia CEO as a fine person. "I hope everything's fine. He's done such an incredible job," he added.Asked whether he believed he should have acted on the intelligence after being briefed about it, Trump said: "No, I don't think so. I think he's an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for ⁠it. You have to hear it."The New York Times reported that Trump had been briefed on the intelligence findings approximately a year ago but decided against taking action based on the information.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang acknowledged that he had been unfaithful to his wife but did not provide details about the relationship. The New York Times reported last month that Huang had been involved in a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed. US authorities investigated Alice Huang and concluded that she was an asset of Chinese intelligence.

Article Title: HSBC upgrades Indian equities to 'overweight', downgrades Chinese stocks to 'neutral'
Article Text:
HSBC upgrades Indian equities

Banks, industrials and discretionary consumption among preferred bets

China loses overweight status

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market and other asset classes given by experts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India)

NEW DELHI: India's prolonged stock market correction appears to have made its equities more attractive to global investors, with HSBC raising its rating on the market to 'overweight' from 'neutral'. The global financial services firm cited resilient earnings, improving growth prospects and a reset in valuations as reasons behind its more positive stance.In its latest Asia-Pacific equity strategy report, HSBC said India's investment appeal is supported by strong credit growth, improving earnings momentum and policy measures aimed at sustaining economic growth and currency stability.A key factor behind the upgrade is the correction in Indian equity valuations over several years. HSBC said this reset has made valuations more reasonable, particularly among large-cap stocks, after a period in which Indian markets underperformed other emerging markets.There could also be room for more foreign investment in Indian equities. According to the report, just 22 per cent of global emerging market (GEM) funds currently have an overweight position in India, suggesting scope for further allocations.The brokerage also pointed to the resilience of corporate earnings despite challenging macroeconomic conditions."Growth remains resilient despite a series of macro shocks (i.e., higher interest rates and oil)," the report said, adding that the pace of earnings downgrades has become significantly more modest.Another factor supporting India's appeal is its relatively low volatility and the diversification it offers. HSBC said these characteristics are particularly relevant in Asian markets, where artificial intelligence-related stocks are increasingly dominating investment opportunities.HSBC's preferred sectors reflect its positive assessment of India's growth prospects. Banks remain among its favoured segments, with the brokerage pointing to an improved growth outlook.In the industrial space, it identified capital goods, cement, ports and electronic manufacturing services as areas offering opportunities.The brokerage also drew a distinction between consumer discretionary stocks and staples, expressing a preference for the former. Retailers and automobile companies were among its preferred segments within this category.Insurers and hospitals also remained on HSBC's positive list, with the firm highlighting their growth potential despite recent regulatory uncertainties.However, the outlook is not without risks. HSBC flagged elevated crude oil prices and the possibility of an El Niño weather pattern as potential challenges for the Indian economy.The report warned that if energy prices remain high, they could put pressure on domestic demand and the currency. Higher inflation could also weigh on consumption, with rural demand particularly vulnerable.Even so, HSBC does not expect possible earnings downgrades in the coming quarters to be large enough to significantly undermine overall market sentiment.While HSBC has become more positive on India, its assessment of Chinese equities has turned cautious. The brokerage cut its rating on China to 'neutral' from 'overweight', citing a lack of triggers for a sustained improvement in market valuations.This comes despite attractive valuations and recent policy support. HSBC said weak consumer confidence, persistent difficulties in the property market and softer domestic investment continue to pose challenges to China's growth outlook.Investor activity also points to weaker appetite for Chinese equities. The report highlighted subdued southbound investment flows and declining margin financing, while noting that there are no clear signs of meaningful near-term policy support to strengthen underlying economic growth."Our downgrade reflects our belief that there are limited catalysts that can drive a sustained re-rating," the report said.Despite the downgrade, HSBC continues to see opportunities in select Chinese sectors. Its preferences include banks, consumer stocks offering attractive bond yields, biotechnology and technology hardware companies expected to benefit from the rollout of artificial intelligence.
Article Summary: HSBC raises its rating on the market to 'overweight' from 'neutral' The global financial services firm cited resilient earnings, improving growth prospects and a reset in valuations as reasons behind its more positive stance. Just 22 per cent of global emerging market (GEM) funds currently have an overweight position in India.

Article Title: Mumbai AQI 30% better than last Diwali's, but plunges at night
Article Text:
Diwali celebrations in Mumbai this year experienced a notable improvement in air quality compared to last year.

The city's Air Quality Index registered a 30% enhancement, reaching 132 on Sunday.

‘Awareness drives, court orders pushed noise levels down’

TOI





MUMBAI: Diwali celebrations began with the city enjoying much cleaner air over last year's but the quality plunged to poor/hazardous at several places amid the firecracker-bursting. In the murk glistened a thin silver lining: firecracker noise levels are down compared to two decades ago, coinciding with increasing use of green crackers and more public awareness.The city's AQI was 132 on Sunday, almost a 30% improvement from the 188 recorded during the same period last year. But the PM 2.5 level that stood at a 42 in Andheri at 8pm, soared to 597 just 2 hours later; it was 606 at Malad. Chembur had a PM10 level of 480 at 10pm.Environmental activists caution noise pollution too remains well above permissible limits in many residential areas and stricter enforcement is needed. "So far, the overall noise levels are lower than previous years. But one needs to check if firecrackers are burst late Sunday night," said anti-noise pollution activist Sumaira Abdulali of Awaaz Foundation.A recent study by Awaaz Foundation and Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) found peak firecracker noise levels have fallen sharply over the last 20 years (see box).RTI activist Anil Galgali agreed noise levels were lower, crediting awareness campaigns and court orders.Peak readings during a pre-Diwali testing of firecrackers this year touched 93 decibels (dB), substantially lower than the 144.9 dB recorded in 2006, a recent Awaaz Foundation and MPCB study showed.While the Mumbai and Thane District Fireworks Dealers Welfare Association described this year’s cracker sales as “largely normal”, several retailers across the city reported a decline in demand compared to previous years.According to association’s honorary general secretary Minesh N Mehta, firecracker sales had dropped to around 70% by the end of Ganeshotsav, but business picked up through Navratri and Diwali after an initially slow start. “Most crackers available today are green crackers and consumers have accepted them over the last five years. Sales have been broadly normal, though trends vary from area to area,” Mehta said.However, traders on the ground painted a more nuanced picture. A Vile Parle dealer said sales were lower than last year as many customers deliberately reduced purchases owing to environmental concerns. A Malad shop owner noted that children themselves were urging parents to buy fewer crackers and opt for green varieties such as sparklers and ground spinners. Bombay High Court had also recently ruled that celebrities should voluntarily help spread awareness against firecracker pollution without charging any public moneyspoke to residents, activists and political leaders attributing the change to greater environmental awareness and compliance with court directions. RTI activist Anil Galgali said noise levels were lower, crediting awareness drives and court orders, though political events in some areas may have caused localised spikes.Andheri resident Karan Jotwani said both cracker sales and bursting had visibly declined in the Lokhandwala area. “The number of cracker stalls has reduced and even in my 240-flat housing society, noise was nearly half of previous years. I also think people are becoming more conscious. I was especially worried as I have a pet at home now,” he said.Shiv Sena corporator Amey Ghole said greater public awareness had encouraged many people to either avoid crackers or opt for green fireworks. “So, there was more focus on the traditional and environmentally friendly options this Diwali. The celebrations were more cultural and less loud which is a welcome move. We are all for celebrations that are environmentally friendly,” Ghole said. BJP MLA Mihir Kotecha said most citizens followed the HC directive by bursting crackers within housing complexes and grounds rather than on public roads.Former Congress corporator Sheetal Mhatre also observed a decline in cracker noise, adding that rising living costs and higher cracker prices may have prompted many households to cut back on purchases this year.But Abdulali pointed out that even 93 dB exceeds prescribed ambient noise limits for residential, commercial, industrial and silence zones. In a representation to the state govt, she urged authorities to strengthen enforcement of noise regulations, particularly during Diwali. In her letter to CM Devendra Fadnavis, she also highlighted that Mumbai has 110 notified silence zones where bursting firecrackers is prohibited. Firecrackers are banned between 10 pm and 6 am across the city.
Article Summary: The city's AQI was 132 on Sunday, almost a 30% improvement from the 188 recorded during the same period last year. But the PM 2.5 level that stood at a 42 in Andheri at 8pm, soared to 597 just 2 hours later. A recent study found peak firecracker noise levels have fallen sharply over the last 20 years.

Article Title: Delhi's air quality slips into 'severe' category on Diwali, AQI hits 404; Mumbai 30% better than last year
Article Text:
Data shared by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) showed that the air quality monitoring station at ITO recorded an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 406.

Delhi's pollution levels cross 400 at several monitoring stations

GRAP Stage III restrictions already in force across Delhi-NCR

Mumbai at '170'

What are the different stages of GRAP?

How is AQI classified?

(With inputs from ANI)





NEW DELHI: A day after Diwali celebrations, air quality across the national capital continued to deteriorate, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) slipping into the 'severe' category in parts of Delhi in the early hours on Monday, according to data shared by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).Hazy conditions and reduced visibility were reported across parts of the national capital, raising fresh concerns over the impact of post-festival pollution.The smog was particularly visible around Inderlok, while several other parts of the city also woke up to poor visibility and deteriorating air quality.According to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), Ghazipur recorded an AQI of 418, placing it in the 'severe' category, while the reading around Akshardham stood at 337, categorised as 'very poor'.Several monitoring stations across Delhi reported AQI readings above 400. Burari Crossing recorded the highest reading at 441, followed by Vivek Vihar at 437, Delhi Technological University (DTU) at 434, North Campus of Delhi University and Jahangirpuri at 433 each, and Rohini at 430.Other locations in the 'severe' category included Mundka at 417, Punjabi Bagh at 409, NIH Narela at 407 and ITO at 407.Among other monitoring stations, CRRI Mathura Road recorded an AQI of 396, Aya Nagar 386, Talkatora Garden 384, NSUT Jaffarpur 378, Lodhi Road 370, Mandir Marg 369, Wazirpur 365, R K Puram 364, Badarpur 363, IHBAS Dilshad Garden 363 and Dr Karni Singh Shooting Range 361.Najafgarh recorded an AQI of 340, Anand Vihar 335, IMD Lodhi Road 323, Ashok Vihar 319 and Sri Aurobindo Marg 267. Data for IIT Delhi and Dwarka Sector 8 was unavailable.The deterioration comes after the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) invoked Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across Delhi-NCR on Friday, three days before Diwali, amid concerns over a further deterioration in pollution levels.The emergency measures are aimed at preventing air quality from worsening further through additional restrictions, increased enforcement and pollution-control measures.The action plan covers Delhi and adjoining districts of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. It is invoked as a precautionary measure based on meteorological and pollution forecasts provided by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), allowing restrictions to be implemented before citywide AQI levels reach the 'severe' category.Meanwhile, Mumbai also witnessed hazy conditions on Monday, with a thick layer of smog blanketing Kalanagar and Bandra areas.The city's AQI stood at 170 on Monday morning, placing it in the 'moderate' category.According to monitoring data, Kherwadi-Bandra East recorded an AQI of 264, followed by Sewri at 226, Ghatkopar at 221 and Chembur at 216.Byculla recorded an AQI of 193, Mindspace-Malad West 191, Kandivali West 187 and Worli 148. Kurla recorded an AQI of 96.In Uttar Pradesh, a thick layer of smog blanketed Lucknow as several parts of the city woke up to hazy conditions.GRAP is a four-stage emergency framework managed by the CAQM in coordination with the CPCB and regional state governments. Restrictions become progressively stricter as air quality deteriorates.Under Stage I, triggered when the AQI is between 201 and 300 and categorised as 'poor', the focus is on controlling road dust, enforcing pollution norms and prohibiting open waste burning.Stage II comes into force when the AQI is between 301 and 400, categorised as 'very poor'. It entails enhanced dust-control measures, higher parking fees and staggered office timings.Stage III is invoked when the AQI reaches the 401-450 range, classified as 'severe'. It includes stricter vehicle restrictions, a halt to construction activities and hybrid learning arrangements for primary school students.Stage IV, applicable when the AQI exceeds 450 and enters the 'severe plus' category, involves restrictions on heavy goods vehicles and emergency measures targeting traffic and industrial pollution.According to CPCB classification, an AQI between 0 and 50 is considered 'good', 51-100 'satisfactory', 101-200 'moderate', 201-300 'poor', 301-400 'very poor' and 401-500 'severe'.
Article Summary: Hazy conditions and reduced visibility reported across parts of the national capital. Ghazipur recorded an AQI of 418, while the reading around Akshardham stood at 337, categorised as'very poor' Burari Crossing recorded the highest reading at 441, followed by Vivek Vihar at 437. Mumbai also witnessed hazy conditions on Monday, with a thick layer of smog blanketing Kalanagar and Bandra areas.

Article Title: Gujarati-origin man indicted in US over $2m Ponzi scheme
Article Text:
A Gujarati-origin man named Kevin Patel has been indicted by a federal grand jury for wire fraud (Representative image)





AHMEDABAD: A Gujarati-origin man who allegedly duped investors in the US through a Ponzi scheme involving nearly $2 million has been indicted by a federal grand jury in New Hampshire on charges of wire fraud.This marks a fresh development in a case that had earlier drawn the attention of state securities regulators in the US.Kevin Patel, who founded and operated Royal Investments LLC, allegedly solicited investments from people across the US by promising to invest their money in the stock market and guarantee annual returns of 12% to 16%, according to an indictment filed in the US district court for New Hampshire on Nov 4.The indictment alleges that Patel founded the company in 2018 and marketed it as "The Company of Wealth & Trust".Investors were promised quarterly interest payments and a full return of their principal at the end of fixed investment terms, with assurances that they would suffer no losses.However, prosecutors allege that Royal Investments was a Ponzi scheme in which almost none of the investors' funds were actually invested.Instead, the money was allegedly diverted towards personal expenses, payments to family members and repayment of earlier investors using funds collected from new investors.The alleged scheme operated from at least Feb 2020 until April 2026. Patel allegedly ran out of funds towards the end of 2024 and stopped making interest and principal payments, leaving investors with losses running into several hundred thousand dollars.The indictment cites three wire transfers - $50,000 from New Jersey in March 2023 and two transfers of $50,000 and $30,000 from Florida in Nov and Dec 2023 - as specific instances of the alleged fraud.The latest federal action follows proceedings initiated by New Hampshire securities regulators in Dec 2025.The state had accused Patel and Royal Investments of operating without the required licences and allegedly defrauding four investors of nearly $386,000. Regulators had sought restitution, penalties and a permanent ban on securities-related activities.The federal indictment charges Patel with three counts of wire fraud. The allegations are yet to be proved in court.
Article Summary: Gujarati-origin Kevin Patel has been indicted by a federal grand jury for wire fraud. He allegedly duped investors in the US through a Ponzi scheme involving nearly $2 million. This marks a fresh development in a case that had earlier drawn the attention of state securities regulators.

Article Title: Delay in moving garbage depot from Pune's Kothrud raises a stink
Article Text:
Residents living near Kothrud garbage depot continue to suffer from overpowering odours affecting their daily lives (Photo credit: Aditya Waikul)

Assault on senses

More about the depot

Road to a nightmare

Focus on decentralisation





PUNE: The Kothrud garbage depot makes it presence felt long before it comes into view, with its stench wafting for several meters around it.The all-pervasive odour is not just a perennial pain point for residents in the vicinity, but also for commuters plying on the stretch, more so because of the overflowing leachate rendering the road a slippery mess.The depot was technically handed over by Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) to Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation Limited (Maha Metro) for a maintenance yard and commercial building back in 2019. However, the lack of alternative premises around where garbage can be segregated has prolonged the depot’s use — making it a never-ending issue for residents.Kothrud garbage depot was established in the 1970s, but nearby residents said the stench is a byproduct of more recent times and is only getting worse by the year.“We have now been forced to become accustomed to the smell. There is also a drainage issue here adding to the stink,” said Vilas Chavan, who has lived behind the depot for over 30 years.“Many people own homes here and renting elsewhere would be expensive,” the retired real estate agent added.Ameya Balkawade, who lives on the opposite side of the depot said, “We have thought about leaving and finding a home elsewhere many times, but not only would the cost be huge, selling property here has become difficult because of the smell and dirt.It’s not easy now. The situation was a lot better when the depot had not been handed over to Maha Metro. Since then, all the waste is segregated on the roadside and not inside.”The advocate added, “The situation deteriorates in the monsoon. Waste mixes with rainwater and forms leachate, making the road slippery and worsening the odour. In 2019, when the city saw flooding, all the waste flowed into our homes from across the road, since we are at a slightly lower level than the depot.”At the time of the handover, PMC had also arranged to shift waste management from the depot to another site in Bavdhan. However, because of land acquisition hurdles, waste continues to be segregated at the Kothrud depot, but only on the ramp.Residents said the current space is inadequate as the population in the area has risen exponentially, not just because of rampant redevelopment in Kothrud but also innumerable projects coming up across Bavdhan.Owing to this, one can find trash scattered across several main roads and bylanes in localities of Kothrud, Bavdhan, Paud Road, Warje and neighbouring areas, but garbage trucks filled to the brim are also always stationed outside the depot.The heavy vehicle density plying on the stretch reduces available road width, while waste and water drip from trucks, making the road slippery and dirty.Accidents have become a common feature here and many commuters tend to avoid the route, choosing to take a longer way to their destinations.“Riding a two-wheeler here, especially when it is raining, is dangerous,” said Raksha Chowdhary, an insurance advisor and real estate property manager. “I often travel from Bavdhan to Vanaz Metro station. Whether I take my two-wheeler, go by auto or in a car, the stench is overpowering. There were so many plans for this depot, all in the works for years now — but we can’t see any change,” she added.Another commuter, business consultant and Bavdhan resident Ashutosh Sathe, said, “Dirty water leaking from garbage trucks makes the road surface oily, smelly and slippery. Riding a bike here is very risky. I have seen multiple two-wheelers sliding, resulting in injuries.”Meanwhile, work on the Vanaz-Chandni Chowk Metro extension is also going on here. “This work has further narrowed the carriageway width. Large garbage trucks and cars get stuck in traffic snarls for hours on end. Between the horrible smell, slippery surface, heavy dust clouds, and endless traffic delays, this route has become nothing but a headache,” added Sathe.Santosh Varule, deputy commissioner of PMC’s solid waste management department, said, “We are working to decentralise the system and are in the process of identifying smaller spaces, where lesser amounts of waste can be segregated and then transferred or processed. The depot is important and closing it will have a big impact on the waste management system of the entire area.”He added, “The alternative site in Bavdhan was not large enough as the quantity of waste generated in collection areas has increased. There is no other option right now to move the waste transfer station on an urgent basis. There is also no other depot nearby to send the vehicles to either. We are trying to reduce the burden on Kothrud depot and move collected waste in instalments. If waste is taken to the processing site directly, the cost of running vehicles will increase exponentially. ”Experts in the field agree. Manju Tadwalkar, director of Inora Biotech, an environment solutions company, said, “Decentralisation is crucial for resolving the bottlenecks seen at overloaded facilities like the Kothrud depot. By processing wet waste at the bulk-generator level, (housing societies and commercial hubs), up to 50–60% of municipal waste would never enter the transportation pipeline. It would also reduces the number of heavy vehicles queued on main road and eliminate carriageway blockages, leachate spillage, and road safety hazards. ”Listing out further solutions, Tadwalkar added, “PMC officials can implement localised depot management strategies like integrating waste planning in the redevelopment plan in a bid to tackle spillage, road congestion and odour. They have already done this, but on-ground inspections need to be done to verify if it is being followed.”“They must also use microbial sprays at the depot site to instantly break down odour-causing organic compounds and control stench as well as implement strict time slots for collection trucks to avoid queueing. These trucks must have sealed leachate collection trays and covered bodies before entering the public carriageway to stop any kind of spillage,” she added.
Article Summary: Kothrud garbage depot was established in the 1970s, but residents say the stench is a byproduct of more recent times. The depot was technically handed over by Pune Municipal Corporation to Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation Limited (Maha Metro) for a maintenance yard and commercial building back in 2019.

Article Title: Crackers versus vehicles: What really contributes to Delhi's Diwali pollution?
Article Text:
Vehicles and transport emissions contributed 19% to Delhi’s PM2.5 pollution on the day of the festival, November 8

Diwali fireworks add to existing pollution

Vehicles: An endless source

Diwali fireworks release fine particles that rapidly worsen air quality

Crackers push particulate levels sharply higher

Low wind speeds and temperature inversion make it harder to disperse pollutants

What crackers bring to the table

Delhi's PM2

Weather is the difference

Can't ignore either one





Every year, Delhi’s Diwali pollution debate is between two sources: firecrackers and vehicles. But the latest pollution data suggests the problem is more complex. Pollution can spike sharply in the case of fireworks, but vehicles are one of the biggest contributors to the city’s everyday PM2.5 burden.The real worry is what will happen when these emissions combine with an atmosphere that is already polluted and with bad weather.The Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) has set up a new Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory (AATAL), which gives a useful picture of Delhi’s pollution mix.Vehicles were the single largest contributor to the city’s PM2.5 pollution on Oct. 24, accounting for 25%. Secondary organic aerosols contributed 18.4 %, followed by secondary inorganic aerosols (16.5 %), road dust (10.9 %) and waste burning (5 %).Even around Diwali the transport contribution was still substantial. Vehicles and transport emissions contributed 19% to Delhi’s PM2.5 pollution on the day of the festival, November 8, the largest identified source, estimated the IITM’s Decision Support System (DSS).The figure explains why vehicular pollution cannot be seen as a seasonal problem: unlike fireworks, traffic emissions persist throughout the year.But firecrackers cause pollution of a different kind of episode. They tend to emit their emissions over a relatively short period of time, and they emit fine particles and gasses that can quickly degrade air quality.The effect was visible on the night of Diwali. The Delhi Pollution Control Committee’s data reported on November 9 showed that at Akshardham the PM2.5 concentration was at 760.99 micrograms per cubic meter at 11pm. This was an hourly reading, not a 24 hour average, but gives an idea of how intense the spike of pollution was.Delhi’s AQI had already fallen to 382 on November 6, its worst pre-Diwali reading in eight years, according to CPCB data. It averaged 376 on Diwali November 8, from 369 a day earlier. AQI stood at 368 at 7am on November 9. Of the 54 monitoring stations that reported valid readings, 50 were above 300 and 15 entered the severe category.At the time when fireworks are set off, the Delhi atmosphere is becoming less conducive to dispersing pollutants. The Air Quality Early Warning System said dispersion is difficult when ventilation index is less than 6,000 square meters per second and average wind speeds are below 10kmph. Low temperatures and temperature inversion can also trap pollutants near the ground.That means fireworks smoke doesn’t just disappear when the party’s over. It adds to the existing emissions from vehicles, industry, dust and regional sources, thus adding to the particulate load.The latest figures do not allow for simply blaming either crackers or vehicles. Fireworks are a concentrated blast of pollution to an already stressed atmosphere, but cars carry the burden of emissions daily. Cracker restrictions can curb the festive spike, but sustained improvement will depend on curbing transport emissions, controlling road dust and industrial pollution, and improving regional coordination. One night of action cannot fix a year-long problem of air pollution in Delhi.
Article Summary: Vehicles were the single largest contributor to the city’s PM2.5 pollution on Oct. 24, accounting for 25%. Secondary organic aerosols contributed 18.4 %, followed by secondary inorganic aerosols (16.5%) and road dust (10.9%) Fireworks are a concentrated blast of pollution to an already stressed atmosphere, but cars carry the burden of emissions daily.

Article Title: Samsung set to become South Korea's first company with 200 trillion won in cash
Article Text:
Samsung's cash reserves to cross 200 trillion won as AI chip demand grows

Samsung Electronics is on course to become the first company in South Korea to build cash assets of more than 200 trillion won ($146.6 billion), with the artificial intelligence (AI)-driven semiconductor boom strengthening its financial position.The chipmaker's cash reserves have nearly doubled over the past year, while its overall assets have also grown. The increase comes as Samsung prepares for higher investments in semiconductor manufacturing and research, alongside a sizeable shareholder return programme.Samsung's cash and cash equivalents are estimated to have reached 214.8 trillion won by the end of the third quarter, according to industry data released on Sunday. This marks a rise of 24.8 trillion won from the 190 trillion won recorded at the end of the previous quarter, as reported by Yonhap news agency.The latest estimate is also almost twice the 108.5 trillion won the company held at the end of the third quarter of 2025.Samsung's total assets stood at 791.8 trillion won at the end of September, an increase of 32.4 trillion won over the preceding three months.The company's growing cash position is expected to be enough to cover the highest possible payout under its landmark shareholder return policy announced in August, market watchers estimate.Samsung had indicated that it would make between 90 trillion won and 110 trillion won available for shareholder returns in 2026.The company is also expected to announce its shareholder policy for the coming year at a board meeting scheduled for January.Alongside shareholder payouts, Samsung is preparing for a significant increase in spending on its semiconductor business.Investments in chipmaking infrastructure and research and development are expected to exceed 100 trillion won this year, marking a historic high. Of this amount, 84.4 trillion won is expected to go towards expanding its memory production facilities.Samsung expects the semiconductor supercycle to extend through next year, supported by continued investments in artificial intelligence and a crunch in memory supply.
Article Summary: Samsung's cash and cash equivalents are estimated to have reached 214.8 trillion won by the end of the third quarter, according to industry data released on Sunday. The increase comes as Samsung prepares for higher investments in semiconductor manufacturing and research, alongside a sizeable shareholder return programme.

Article Title: Rupee extends winning streak, breaks below 94 against dollar: What's next
Article Text:
Rupee moves below 94 against US dollar

Crude oil prices cool as hopes of peace grow

Foreign fund inflows add to rupee's support

NEW DELHI: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. The rally was supported by softer crude oil prices, stronger foreign fund inflows and hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East.The currency rose 24 paise to 93.74 against the US dollar in early trade. It opened at around 93.85 in the interbank forex market before gaining further. Rupee had already made a strong recovery on Friday, rising 43 paise to close at 93.98 against the greenback.Forex traders said rupee could maintain its positive momentum if diplomatic efforts in the Middle East make progress. Any easing of tensions could reduce the risk premium in crude oil prices, providing further support to the currency.These hopes gained ground over the weekend after US President Donald Trump indicated that further military strikes against Iran were highly unlikely if negotiations progressed and both sides reached a strong agreement.The easing in crude oil prices has been one of the key factors supporting rupee. Brent crude, which had earlier climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. Amit Pabari, managing director of CR Forex Advisors, said improving diplomatic expectations were already having an impact on energy prices."The improvement in diplomatic expectations is already reflecting in energy prices. Brent crude, which had climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. For currency markets, even the possibility of a lasting agreement is important," Pabari said.Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.15% lower at $98.17 per barrel in futures trade. The dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was also down 0.12% at 102.18.Foreign investment activity provided another source of support for the domestic currency. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) purchased equities worth Rs 13,749.82 crore on Friday, according to exchange data.The combination of lower crude prices and stronger foreign fund inflows has supported the rupee's recent gains against the dollar.With rupee now below the 94-per-dollar level, Pabari sees further room for appreciation. He expects the currency to move towards 93.50 and 93.00, while identifying 94.40–94.50 as the immediate resistance zone."With USD/INR breaking below the 94.00 mark, the probability of further rupee appreciation towards 93.50 and 93.00 has increased. On the upside, 94.40–94.50 is likely to act as the immediate resistance zone," Pabari said.Meanwhile, domestic equity markets opened lower on Monday. BSE Sensex fell 93.95 points to 80,919.19, while NSE Nifty declined 30 points to 24,968.80.Separately, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reported that India's foreign exchange reserves declined by $2.691 billion to $717.056 billion in the week ended October 30.
Article Summary: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. The rally was supported by softer crude oil prices, stronger foreign fund inflows and hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East. Rupee had already made a strong recovery on Friday, rising 43 paise to close at 93.98.

Article Title: Meta’s chief strategy officer Dave Wehner is leaving the company for four-year-old AI startup; sends 'right mission' message; says: I have become increasingly ...
Article Text:
From Meta veteran to AI challenger

Fireworks eyes its next phase of growth

AI boom draws senior executives

AI race intensifies

Read Meta chief strategy officer Dave Wehner’s complete post here

Wehner's move underscores the growing pull of the AI industry as startups compete with larger rivals such as OpenAI, Anthropic and major cloud providers.

With fresh capital, rising valuations and growing enterprise demand for AI infrastructure, companies like Fireworks are increasingly attracting experienced leaders who see artificial intelligence as the next major technology platform.

Read Meta chief strategy officer Dave Wehner’s complete post here

I announced earlier this week that I am leaving Meta. I am deeply grateful to Mark Zuckerberg for showing what a truly founder-led company can achieve.

I am incredibly optimistic for Meta’s future.

At Meta, I was able to witness the most exciting opportunities in enterprise AI. That’s why today, I’m announcing that I will be joining Fireworks as CFO. I am thrilled to be joining a founder-led growth company where I can roll up my sleeves and put my experience to work.

Fireworks has the right mission for the moment. Companies will use AI to build on what makes them distinctive: their data and expertise.

Specialized intelligence gives them a way to capture those advantages and own their “alpha.” Open models offer price points that allow the technology to have the greatest impact. Fireworks is building the platform to make all of this possible.

I’ve known and respected Lin

for a long time. As I’ve spent more time with her and the people at Fireworks, I’ve become increasingly bullish on what they are building. There’s a remarkable depth of technical talent here, coupled with a very practical focus on what customers need.

I see AI as the most consequential technology shift of my lifetime. I’m excited to get to work and help build a business at the center of it.

Dave Wehner, Meta’s chief strategy officer and former chief financial officer, is leaving the social media giant to join fast-growing AI startup Lin Qiao-led Fireworks as its new CFO, marking another high-profile move from Big Tech into the artificial intelligence sector. Wehner announced the move in a post on X, saying he had become increasingly convinced of the opportunity ahead for the four-year-old startup. “Fireworks has the right mission for the moment,” he wrote. “I’ve become increasingly bullish on what they are building. There’s a remarkable depth of technical talent here, coupled with a very practical focus on what customers need.” Fireworks, which provides AI inference and model-training services built around open-source AI models, was valued at $17.5 billion in a Series D funding round in July.Wehner joined Meta, then known as Facebook, in 2012 and served as the company’s chief financial officer from 2014 to 2022 before taking on the role of chief strategy officer. During his tenure, he helped steer the company through a period of rapid growth, expanding advertising revenues and major bets on new technologies. In a statement to CNBC, Meta COO Javier Olivan praised Wehner's contributions, saying he helped guide the company through “tremendous growth and complexity” over the past 14 years while bringing disciplined thinking to some of its most important strategic decisions.At Fireworks, Wehner will oversee the company's finances and operations as it looks to scale further in the increasingly competitive AI market. CEO Lin Qiao said Wehner's experience would help the company as it enters its next stage of expansion.Founded in 2022 by former Meta and Google employees, Fireworks allows developers and businesses to customise, train and run open AI models. The company counts investors such as Nvidia and Sequoia Capital among its backers and has reportedly held early discussions for another funding round that could value the startup between $30 billion and $40 billion.“Dave told me he wanted to get back to a smaller company where he could build toward a big impact again,” Qiao wrote in a LinkedIn post. “He sees AI as the defining technology shift of his lifetime and wants to help shape what comes next.”Wehner's departure comes as venture-backed AI companies continue to attract seasoned executives from some of the world's largest technology firms. While Fireworks remains significantly smaller than Meta, which had a market capitalisation of about $1.56 trillion at Friday's close, the startup is positioning itself as a key player in the market for open AI models.The company has also faced challenges associated with rapid growth. In October, Fireworks disclosed a security incident involving unauthorised use of internal credentials that allowed limited access to environment variables used in evaluation jobs within a small number of customer accounts. The company said its investigation found no evidence of unauthorised access to customer models, datasets, training data, personal information or inference traffic.Wehner's move underscores the growing pull of the AI industry as startups compete with larger rivals such as OpenAI, Anthropic and major cloud providers. With fresh capital, rising valuations and growing enterprise demand for AI infrastructure, companies like Fireworks are increasingly attracting experienced leaders who see artificial intelligence as the next major technology platform.
Article Summary: Dave Wehner, Meta’s chief strategy officer and former chief financial officer, is leaving the social media giant to join fast-growing AI startup Fireworks. Wehner announced the move in a post on X, saying he had become increasingly convinced of the opportunity ahead for the four-year-old startup. Fireworks provides AI inference and model-training services built around open-source AI models.

Article Title: Google executive Donald Harrison has resigned from SpaceX board with immediate effect; CEO Elon Musk says: At this point, there are simply too many ...
Article Text:
Elon Musk sends 'let's go to Space' message hours after mid-term election results

Elon Musk's Spacex has announced the departure of its longtime Google executive Donald Harrison. In an SEC filing the company said that Harrison has resigned from the rocket maker’s board of directors. Harrison is an old-timer at Google. He has worked at Google since 2005, and is the search giant’s president of global partnerships and corporate development. SpaceX thanked Harrison for his “many contributions and his years of dedicated and outstanding service” to the company.Spacex founder and CEO Elon Musk too responded to a post on Harrison leaving the company's board. "Don has been a great board member. Very much appreciate his contributions. At this point, there are simply too many conflicts of interest with ...," wrote Musk.In a statement on Harrison leaving Spacex board, Google said, “While Don is stepping down from the board, we remain deeply supportive of SpaceX’s mission and are excited to continue our long-standing partnership.”Spacex SEC filing on Donald Harrison's exitIn its SEC filing, Spacex said, "On November 4, 2026, Donald Harrison, a Class B Director of Space Exploration Technologies Corp.(the “Company”), notified the Company of his intention to resign as a member of the Board of Directors (the “Board”), effective immediately. Mr. Harrison’s decision to resign was not due to any disagreement with the Company on any matter relating to its operations, policies, or practices. The Company and the Board express their deep appreciation to Mr. Harrison for his many contributions and his years of dedicated and outstanding service to the Company, and wish him the very best in his future endeavors."Google's relationship with SpacexThe announcement comes roughly five months after SpaceX went public in what has been the largest IPO on record. Google parent Alphabet maintains close ties with SpaceX, having invested in Elon Musk’s company in 2015, when it was valued at about $12 billion. Alphabet is now the largest institutional investor n SpaceX, with a stake worth $74 billion as of Friday’s close. SpaceX’s current market cap is about $1.8 trillion.Elon Musk responded with a single word 'Interesting', on Google buying more Spacex sharesIn January 2015, Google invested $900 million as part of a $1 billion funding round alongside Fidelity, backing Spacex's ambitions in reusable rockets and satellite communications. Google is a key customer of Spacex, and has agreed to pay the company’s AI division up to $920 million a month for compute capacity from its data centers in the area around Memphis, Tennessee. The companies also recently worked together to launch Google AI chips into orbit via Project Suncatcher.Google-parent Alphabet ) recently expanded its Spacex stake by nearly 4 million additional shares, lifting the holding's value to about $69 billion. Google's parent company held approximately 555 million SpaceX shares at the end of September, up from 551.2 million three months earlier as per Reuters.
Article Summary: Elon Musk's Spacex has announced the departure of its longtime Google executive Donald Harrison. In an SEC filing the company said that Harrison has resigned from the rocket maker’s board of directors. Harrison is an old-timer at Google, and has worked at the search giant since 2005. SpaceX thanked Harrison for his “many contributions and his years of dedicated and outstanding service”

Article Title: Uber shares one number to tell everyone, how 'unpopular' AI Agents may be on its platform
Article Text:
Few hundreds from millions

Tech giants and venture capitalists have spent billions hyping the rise of autonomous personal AI agents. They are selling or rather promising a future where software handles everyday tasks like hailing rides and ordering food. But it seems that in the real-world, consumers are still tapping their own screens. During Uber’s third-quarter earnings call, executives disclosed that only four rides worldwide were hailed via an AI agent during the week of Halloween — traditionally regarded as the company’s busiest week of the year.Deliveries through Uber Eats saw slightly more activity, but the numbers remained negligible. Uber Chief Financial Officer Balaji Krishnamurthy reported that out of roughly 320 million total trips and food delivery orders completed that week, just 500 meals were ordered using an AI intermediary.“It is very, very early and very limited traction that we are seeing so far,” Uber Chief Executive Officer Dara Khosrowshahi told analysts. “Listen, we hope that there will be more traction.”The negligible adoption highlights a stark divide between Silicon Valley’s ambition and everyday consumer behavior. The race to develop agentic AI has ignited massive funding rounds and corporate repositioning across the tech sector.Technology giants such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and SpaceXAI (developer of Grok) have all rolled out task-oriented assistants. Yet public earnings reports reveal that real-world integration remains almost nonexistent. Just last week, delivery rival DoorDash disclosed on its own earnings call that it had recorded only a few hundred AI-initiated orders, noting that users overwhelmingly stick to native apps.Khosrowshahi attributed the muted adoption to simple efficiency. Booking a ride in the standard Uber app takes an average of 50 seconds, he noted, while reordering a favorite meal takes roughly 90 seconds, this actually leaves little friction for an AI agent to solve.Even so, Uber leadership remains optimistic that the technology will eventually expand the company’s footprint. Khosrowshahi noted that roughly eight major assistants currently populate the market, a figure he expects to surpass 10 as adoption matures. “We think that is another opportunity to reach our platform,” Khosrowshahi said. “We think it will be a net positive in terms of demand on the ecosystem.”
Article Summary: Only four rides were hailed via an AI agent during the week of Halloween. Uber Eats saw slightly more activity, but the numbers remained negligible. The negligible adoption highlights a stark divide between Silicon Valley’s ambition and everyday consumer behavior. The race to develop agentic AI has ignited massive funding rounds.

Article Title: Delhi's Diwali fire rush: 257 emergency calls, 85 in just 2 hours as blazes erupt across city
Article Text:
Delhi Fire Service received 257 emergency calls during Diwali this year, which marks a decline from last year





DELHI: Delhi Fire Service (DFS) received 257 emergency calls on Diwali this year, including 214 fire-related calls and 24 incidents involving cracker fires.While the city witnessed several major blazes at factories, a godown, a banquet hall and residential premises, the overall number of emergency calls registered a decline compared to last year, when the department received 269 calls.Abhilash Kumar Malik, chief fire officer of DFS , the highest number of calls was recorded between 8pm and 10pm on November 8, when the fire department received 85 calls, including 84 fire-related calls and eight cracker-fire incidents.Between 10pm and midnight, another 61 calls were received, of which 60 were fire-related and 10 involved cracker fires.The department recorded 16 calls between midnight and 7am, 36 between 7am and 2pm, 14 between 2pm and 4pm, 13 between 4pm and 6pm and 32 between 6pm and 8pm.Most of these calls were related to fire.
Article Summary: Delhi Fire Service received 257 emergency calls on Diwali this year, including 214 fire-related calls and 24 incidents involving cracker fires. While the city witnessed several major blazes at factories, a godown, a banquet hall and residential premises, the overall number of emergency calls registered a decline compared to last year.

Article Title: BMC bans rockets, aerial firecrackers across Mumbai till November 25 after spate of fire incidents
Article Text:
The ban covers both public and private spaces, including residential buildings, terraces, balconies, courtyards





MUMBAI: In the wake of a spate of firecracker-related fires across Mumbai over the past two days, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) on Monday imposed a blanket ban on the use of rockets and other sky-flying firecrackers across the city till November 25.The prohibitory order, issued by municipal commissioner Prajakta Lavangare-Verma in her capacity as chairperson (in-charge) of the Urban Disaster Management Authority, Brihanmumbai, came into immediate effect on November 9 and will remain in force until 11.59 pm on November 25.The ban covers both public and private spaces, including residential buildings, terraces, balconies, courtyards, parking lots, slum areas and all other premises within the BMC limits.The order cites the risk posed by burning remnants of rockets and other aerial firecrackers falling on building rooftops, balconies, windows and other inflammable materials, potentially triggering fires.Given Mumbai’s dense population, high-rise buildings, congested slum settlements, narrow roads and closely packed commercial and residential structures, such incidents could pose a serious threat to life and property, it states.The BMC has invoked provisions of the Disaster Management Act, 2005, including Sections 41(A), 26(2), 30 and 34(M), to enforce the preventive ban.Zonal deputy commissioners of police, the BMC’s divisional assistant commissioners and the fire brigade have been directed to ensure its implementation. The civic body’s public relations officer has also been asked to give the order wide publicity.Clarifying the scope of the restrictions, the order states that the use of firecrackers other than rockets and similar sky-flying crackers will continue to be governed by existing laws, orders issued by competent authorities and directions of the courts.The move comes after the Mumbai Fire Brigade received 142 fire calls on November 8 alone, of which 137 were attributed to firecrackers. Several major fires, including those at Dongri and Vidyavihar, were reported amid the surge in emergencies, putting considerable pressure on firefighting resources.
Article Summary: The ban covers both public and private spaces, including residential buildings, terraces, balconies, courtyards, parking lots, slum areas. The move comes after the Mumbai Fire Brigade received 142 fire calls on November 8 alone, of which 137 were attributed to firecrackers.

Article Title: Thrown out of window due to FSI rule, balconies now a luxury in Mumbai
Article Text:
Balconies were once common in Mumbai housing but have significantly dwindled due to new regulations.

Demand for flats with balcony rose during Covid

Designed for heat

Post-pandemic shift





For most of his life, 36-year-old Mohsin Mulla has enjoyed hanging out in the verandah of his small flat on the top floor of an old Mazgaon building. He could step out with a cup of tea, gaze up at the sky or down at the street, and take a private call. But a year ago, his building was demolished. His temporary digs don’t have a balcony, and neither will the flat he’ll get in his redeveloped building.“The balcony is a luxury now,” he says. Once a common feature of Mumbai housing, the balcony has largely vanished from middle-class buildings, due to a 2012 rule change that brought them into floor space index (FSI) calculations, making them an officially chargeable area. While the change was intended to end malpractice—homeowners enclosed the open area and builders charged buyers for FSI-free space—it also turned the balcony into an expensive extra in a city of sky-high real-estate prices.“The rule changed the calculus of providing balconies for most new tall buildings, leaving them out or reducing them to mere ledges,” says senior architect Moayyed Fatehi. Meanwhile, the outdoor space is now marketed as a premium amenity—called ‘decks’, ‘skydecks’, or terraces, depending on size and design—to woo buyers of prime upper-floor flats or units in luxury complexes.While there has been some post-pandemic pushback—some builders now offer balcony options in small homes—for the most part, Fatehi says, “small flats need balconies the most but get them least.”Historically, balconies were an important climate-responsive feature in a dense tropical city. They reduce heat entering the home—the wall-size glass windows in new towers do just the opposite—and offer a sense of open space in a city without enough parks. They can be seen in buildings across eras, from the wooden balconies of East Indian homes to the galleries of early twentieth-century chawls. Reinforced cement concrete enabled deeper cantilevered balconies in 1940s Art Deco apartments, notes Fatehi, a feature retained in early high-rises of the 1970s and ’80s.By then, balconies had become spaces of contentious regulation. “There’s been a lot of flip and flop on balcony rules,” says veteran liaison architect Manoj Daisaria. He recalls that balconies were once allowed to run the length of a room but were restricted to half that length in the 1970s to prevent enclosures. Authorities tried to include balconies in FSI in the mid-1970s but the effort failed, and they remained exempt up to 10% of floor area until 2012. (See timeline.)Since the rule change, architects have struggled to persuade developers to offer balconies in smaller flats. “Buyers of flats of 350-450 square feet cannot really afford a balcony per today’s real estate prices,” says architect Vilas Nagalkar. “Beyond 800-1000-sq-ft, you’re more likely to see them.”He and other architects estimate that only 20% of new projects offer balconies, and these tend to be in larger suburban complexes. “There’s more scope for planning in large layouts, and prices are not as high as the island city,” says Nagalkar.Demand for balcony apartments has grown since the COVID-19 pandemic, when people came to value being able to step outside their box. In the lockdown, “we noticed our tiny balcony homes sold faster than others,” says Khushbu Davda, architect and co-founder of Studio Emergence, adding,“Builders caught on quickly.”The shift can be seen in Mulla’s redevelopment project in Mazgaon. While Mulla won’t get a balcony in his rehab flat, the project offers sale flats of 500-sq-ft with a small balcony—-something that wasn’t part of older projects. Similarly, in Runwal Forest, an eleven-tower complex rising in Kanjur Marg, 2BHKs are offered both with and without 40-sq-ft balconies—for a price difference of over Rs 10 lakh.Davda’s firm tries to include balconies in its designs, using an angular facade to provide 35-sq-ft balconies in some stand-alone buildings. “It’s tiny but it’s something,” she says. They even designed a commercial building with a balcony, for workers to take a break. “We were able to show that it serves a bigger purpose than just floor space inside,” she says.In high-rises, balconies can be difficult to maintain against the assault of wind, dust, and pigeons, but Fatehi says good design can reduce those issues. Davda believes the BMC should incentivise balconies again. Builders once notorious for misusing free-of-FSI spaces have mostly fallen in line with the new rules, she notes. Some have also become particular about uniform facades, making illegal alterations less likely.If the BMC doesn’t want to fully exempt balconies from FSI, says Davda, it could count them as half FSI---to make the outdoor space cheaper than the indoor. “Even that would help,” she says. “Balconies can come back.”
Article Summary: Balconies were once common in Mumbai housing but have significantly dwindled due to new regulations. A 2012 rule change brought them into floor space index calculations, making them an officially chargeable area. The outdoor space is now marketed as a premium amenity to woo buyers of prime upper-floor flats or units in luxury complexes.

Article Title: Diwali day AQI down in Mumbai, but PM levels past 600 at night
Article Text: Mumbai: First, the good news: the city registered an overall 29.8% improvement in air quality on Sunday afternoon as compared to Diwali and Lakshmi Puja last year. At 4pm, it logged an air quality index of 132—keeping it in the moderately polluted band—down from 188 during the same period last year.But that was it to cheer. Late night celebrations triggered severe localised pollution spikes across several suburbs, sending particulate matter concentrations skyrocketing past 600 on their respective scales within a matter of hours.Monitoring station data captured exponential surges in specific pockets as the night progressed. In Andheri, PM2.5 levels stood at a moderate 42 at 8pm, but soared to 483 just two hours later. Chembur reported a PM10 level of 480 at 10pm, while Deonar and Malad logged extreme PM10 concentrations of 444 and 408, respectively. Byculla experienced a similar sharp escalation, where PM10 remained at 80 until 9pm before surging nearly five-fold to 395 an hour later. Bandra East, BKC, Shivaji Nagar in Govandi, Borivli and Andheri crossed 400 in localised spikes of PM2.5 and PM10 dust pollution. Fine PM2.5 particles can penetrate deep into lung passageways, while PM10 can cause respiratory and cardiovascular problems.Private portals, too, reported a drastic jump in dust pollution readings from across the city. IQAir registered PM2.5 levels at 237 at Bandra Hill Road, 215 at Juhu, and 165 at the US consulate at BKC. AQI.in logged 597 in Andheri East, 606 in Malad, 654 in Jogeshwari, 595 in Mulund, and 415 in Dadar.Environmental analysts noted that while aggregate citywide averages failed to reflect drastic overall changes during the day, these localised nighttime booms highlighted intense, hyperlocal pollution pockets during festival celebrations.
Article Summary: The city registered an overall 29.8% improvement in air quality on Sunday afternoon as compared to Diwali and Lakshmi Puja last year. At 4pm, it logged an air quality index of 132—keeping it in the moderately polluted band. But late night celebrations triggered severe localised pollution spikes across several suburbs.
